quotes.quote: Bethany is interpreted, the house of obedience, but Bethphage the house of cheek bones, being a place belonging to the priests, for cheek bones in the sacrifices were the right of the priests, as it is commanded in the law. To that place then where obedience is, and where the priests have the possession, our Saviour sends His disciples to loose the ass's colt.

There is a sect among the Jews which is called the sect of the Sadducees: this sect denies "the resurrection of the dead" and supposes that the soul perishes together with the body, and that after death no faculty of perception any longer remains. These men, then, in putting a question to the Lord, made up the tale of the woman with seven husbands, who after her first husband, in order to raise up seed for the former, married a second, and when he had died a third also, and again a fourth, and in this manner arrived at the seventh. The question, therefore, is which of the seven brothers will claim her as his wife "in the resurrection of the dead". Now they proposed this problem, laying a snare for the words of the Savior, at that time when they saw him teaching his disciples about the resurrection.

quotes.quote:
And in commenting on John we have explained, as best we could, concerning the two robbers who were crucified with Christ, who according to Matthew indeed and Mark both reproached him on the cross, but according to Luke, who says that "one of the hanging robbers blasphemed him, saying: You are the Christ; save yourself and us. It is fitting, therefore, that at first indeed both robbers should be understood to have blasphemed the Lord, but after this that one of them was converted…

"And his mercy is unto generations of generations". The "mercy" of God is extended not unto one generation, nor unto two, nor unto three, nor even unto five, but forever "from generation unto generation".

quotes.quote: Likewise also the twelve were reckoned by two and two, as Matthew shows in his enumeration of them. (Matt. 10:2.) For that two should be joined in service, seems from the word of God to be an ancient custom. For God led Israel out of Egypt by the hands of Moses and Aaron. Joshua and Caleb also, united together, appeased the people who had been provoked by the twelve spies. (Numb. 13, 14. Ex. 12.) Hence it is said, A brother assisted by a brother is as a fortified city. (Prov. 18:19. Vulg.)

Mary and Joseph were seeking Jesus "among their kinsfolk" and did not find him; they were seeking him "in the company" and could not find him. They sought him "in the temple", and not simply "in the temple", but with the teachers, and "in the midst of the instructors" they find him. Wherever the teachers may be, there "in the midst of the teachers" Jesus is found, if only the teacher sits "in the temple" and never departs from it. Jesus profited his own teachers, and those whom he seemed to be questioning he taught, speaking "in their midst", and in a certain way he stirred them up to seek out the things they did not know, and to investigate the things which, up to that point, they were unable to know—whether they knew them or were ignorant of them. Jesus, then, is found "in the midst of the teachers", and once found he says to those who sought him: "Why is it that you were seeking me?…

My Lord Jesus was born, and an angel came down from heaven announcing his birth. Let us see, therefore, whom he sought out, that he might announce his coming. He did not come to Jerusalem, he did not seek out the scribes and Pharisees, he did not enter the synagogue of the Jews, but he found "shepherds keeping watch over their flocks" and spoke to them: "Today there is born to you a Savior, who is Christ the Lord".

Do you suppose that the word of the Scriptures signifies nothing more divine, but says only this, that an angel came to the shepherds and spoke to them? Hear, you shepherds of the churches, you shepherds of God, that his angel always comes down from heaven and announces to you: "Today there is born to you a Savior, who is Christ the Lord". For when a famine came upon the people of Israel, i. e. of hearing the word of God, a prophet came to a widow, of whom it is said, For the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband; (Isa. 54:1, Gal. 4:27.) and when he had come, he multiplies her bread and her nourishment.

Hence to what he had said — "no prophet is accepted in his own homeland" — he adds another thing also: "for in truth I say to you, that there were many widows in the days of Elijah in Israel, when heaven was shut up for three years and six months". What he says is this: Elijah was a prophet and was among the people of the Jews; but when he was about to do something wonderful, although there were many widows in Israel, he left them and came "to the widow in Sarepta of Sidon", to a Gentile woman, unfolding a figure of a thing to come — that, when the people of Israel was seized "not with hunger for bread nor with thirst for water, but with hunger for hearing the word of God", he came to the widow, of whom the prophet also bears witness, saying: "many are the children of the deserted woman, more than of her who has a husband", and, when he had come, he multiplies her bread and her food.…

Those who wish to spread over their sins some excuse suppose that no one is without sin, and they make use of the testimony written in Job: "No one is clean from filth, not even if his life upon the earth should be but of a single day; his months, moreover, are numbered". Of this passage they bring forward only the sound, being wholly ignorant of its interpretation. Against them we shall reply briefly, that to be without sin is understood in the Scriptures in two ways: the one, never to have sinned at all; the other, to have ceased from sinning. If, then, they say that he is called without sin who has never sinned, we too agree that no one is without sin, since all of us as human beings have at some time sinned, even though afterward we have pursued virtue. But if they so understand a man not to be without sin as to deny that anyone, after his vices, so betakes himself to the virtues…

But the evil thoughts of men were revealed, that He Who died for us might slay them; for while they were hidden, it was impossible to utterly destroy them. Hence also when we have sinned we ought to say, Mine iniquity have I not hid. (Ps. 32:5.) For if we make known our sins not only to God, but to whoever can heal our wounds, our sins will be blotted out.

Then Simeon says: "and a sword shall pierce through your own soul". What is this sword, which pierced not only through the hearts of others, but even through the heart of Mary? It is plainly written that in the time of the passion all the apostles were scandalized, the Lord himself also saying: "you shall all be scandalized in me this night". Therefore they were all scandalized to such a degree that even Peter, the chief of the apostles, denied him three times. What are we to think — that, while the apostles were scandalized, the mother of the Lord was immune from scandal? If she suffered no scandal at the passion of the Lord, then Jesus did not die for her sins. But if "all have sinned and lack the glory of God, being justified by his grace and redeemed", then surely Mary too was scandalized at that time. quotes.quote: But why was she lowly and cast down, who carried in her womb the Son of God? Consider that lowliness, which in the Scriptures is particularly praised as one of the virtues, is called by the philosophers "modestia." And we also may paraphrase it, that state of mind in which a man instead of being puffed up, casts himself down.

"Because he has looked", she says, "upon the lowliness of his handmaid". Upon what lowliness of Mary did the Lord look? What did the mother of the Savior have that was lowly and cast down, she who bore the Son of God in her womb? So then, when she says: "he has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid", it is as though she had said: "he has looked" upon the justice of his handmaid, "he has looked" upon her temperance, "he has looked" upon her fortitude and wisdom. For it is fitting that God should look upon the virtues. Let someone answer and say: I understand how God looks upon the justice and wisdom of his handmaid; but how he regards her lowliness is not sufficiently clear. Let him who inquires into such things consider that in the Scriptures, properly speaking, one of the virtues is proclaimed as "lowliness" (humility). quotes.quote: For if she had had no husband, soon would the thought have stolen into the Devil's mind, how she who had known no man could be pregnant. It was right that the conception should be Divine, something more exalted than human nature.

quotes.quote: Then there follows: "when the days of their purification were fulfilled, according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem". On account of the purification, he says, "of them". Of whom, "of them"? If it had been written: on account of her purification, that is, of Mary, who had given birth, no question would arise, and we would boldly say that Mary, who was human, had need of purification after childbirth. But now, in that it says: "the days of their purification", it seems to signify not one, but another or several. Did Jesus, then, have need of purification and was he unclean, or defiled with some filth? Perhaps I seem to speak rashly, but I am moved by the authority of the Scriptures. quotes.quote:
Whence knowest thou, Satan, that those things are written? Hast thou read the Prophets, or the oracles of God? Thou hast read them indeed, but not that thyself mightest be the better for the reading, but that from the mere letter thou mightest slay them who are friends to the letter. (2 Cor. 3:6.) Thou knowest that if thou wert to speak from His other books, thou wouldest not deceive.

But mark how wily he is even in this testimony. For he would fain throw a slur upon the glory of the Saviour, as though He needed the assistance of angels, and would stumble were He not supported by their hands. But this was said not of Christ, but of the saints generally; He needs not the aid of angels, Who is greater than angels. But let this teach thee, Satan, that the angels would stumble did not God sustain them; and thou stumblest, because thou refusest to believe in Jesus Christ the Son of God. But…

And at the same time consider how the devil tempts. He does not dare to tempt from any other source than from the divine books, and taking a testimony from the Psalms he says: "If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down. For it is written: that he has commanded his angels concerning you, and in their hands they will lift you up, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone." Whence do you know, O devil, that these things are written? Have you perhaps read the prophets or come to know the divine utterances? Though you be silent, I will answer for you. You have read, not that you yourself might become better from the reading of the holy things, but that from the bare letter you might slay those who are friends of the letter. You know that, if you should wish to speak to him from other volumes, you will not deceive, nor will your assertions be able to have any authority. Thus Marcion…

quotes.quote: or rather let us spread the sails of our souls toward God and beg for the coming of his word, that it may interpret the parable of which it is written: "When you go with your adversary to the ruler on the way, make an effort to be freed from him, lest perhaps he hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and you be cast into prison. Amen I say to you: you will not come out from there until you pay back the very last mite". I see four persons set down: the adversary, the ruler, the judge, the officer. And because the evangelist Matthew seems to have said something similar in that he says: "Be well-disposed toward your adversary while you are on the way with him", I ask whether the meaning is the same or whether there is some kinship, since with Matthew one person is omitted and another is changed. Omitted is the "ruler", and in place of "officer" a "servant"…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 35

quotes.quote: In the word of prophecy, spoken to the Jews alone, the Jewish kingdom only is mentioned, as, The vision of Esaias, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. (Is. 1:1.) But in the Gospel which was to be proclaimed to the whole world, the empire of Tiberius Cæsar is mentioned, who seemed the lord of the whole world. But if the Gentiles only were to be saved, it were sufficient to make mention only of Tiberius, but because the Jews also must believe, the Jewish kingdom therefore, or Tetrarchies, are also introduced, as it follows, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judæa, and Herod tetrarch, &c.

Consider then this, if the bread be not indeed the food of the soul in knowledge, without which it can not be saved, as, for example, the well planned rule of a just life. But the fish is the love of instruction, as to know the constitution of the world, and the effects of the elements, and whatever else besides wisdom treats of. Therefore God does not in the place of bread offer a stone, which the devil wished Christ to eat, nor in the place of a fish does He give a serpent, which the Ethiopians eat who are unworthy to eat fishes. Nor generally in the place of what is nourishing does he give what is not eatable and injurious, which relates to the scorpion and egg.
The name of which village Luke indeed here omits, but John mentions, calling it Bethany. (John 11.)

"And all", it says, "were amazed". At what were they "amazed"? Not at his questions, although these too were marvelous, but "at his answers". For it is one thing to ask, another to answer. He was questioning the teachers, and because at times they could not answer, he himself answered them concerning the things about which he had asked. But that an answer signifies not the alternation of conversing but teaching in the holy scriptures, let the divine law teach you. "Moses spoke, and God answered him by a voice". That answer was concerning the matters about which the Lord was instructing the ignorant Moses. Sometimes Jesus asks, sometimes he answers, and as we said above, although his questioning is marvelous, nevertheless his answering is far more marvelous.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 18

quotes.quote: Zechariah the priest, while he offers incense in the temple, is condemned to silence and holds his peace; indeed, he speaks only by nods, and remains mute right up to the birth of his son John. To what does this history point? The silence of Zechariah is the silence of the prophets among the people of Israel. In no way does God speak to them, and "the word, which in the beginning was God with the Father", has passed over to us, and Christ is not silent to us, though among them he is silent even to this day: for which reason also the prophet Zechariah kept silent. For it is most clearly proved from his very words that he was both a prophet and a priest. But what does this mean, which follows: "he was making signs to them" and made up for the loss of his voice by nods? I think that such works are those which, being without speech and reason, differ in nothing from nods. But where reason…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 5

quotes.quote: (in Prov. 1:1.) But because the Gentiles say that wisdom is a virtue, and define it to be the experience of what is good, evil, and indifferent, or the knowledge of what is and what is not to be done, we must consider whether this word signifies many things, or one. For it is said that God by wisdom prepared the heavens. (Prov. 3:19.) Now it is plain that wisdom is good, because the Lord by wisdom prepared the heavens. It is said also in Genesis, according to the LXX, that the serpent was the wisest animal, wherein He makes wisdom not a virtue, but evil-minded cunning. And it is in this sense that the Lord commended the steward that he had done wisely, that is, cunningly and evilly. And perhaps the word commended was spoken not in the sense of real commendation, but in a lower sense; as when we speak of a man being commended in slight and indifferent matters, and in a certain measure…

Because moreover He was the Son of God, He is found in the midst of the doctors, enlightening and instructing them. But because He was a little child, He is found among them not teaching but asking questions, as it is said, Sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions. And this He did as a duty of reverence, that He might set us an example of the proper behaviour of children, though they be wise and learned, rather to hear their masters than teach them, and not to vaunt themselves with empty boasting. But He asked not that He might learn, but that asking He might instruct. For from the same source of learning is derived both the power of asking and answering wisely, as it follows, All who heard him were astonished at his wisdom.

The heresy of the Sadducees not only denies the resurrection of the dead, but also believes the soul to die with the body. Watching then to entrap our Saviour in His words, they proposed a question just at the time when they observed Him teaching His disciples concerning the resurrection; as it follows, And they asked him, saying, Master, Moses wrote to us, If a brother, &c.

But if we indeed hear "the word" and from the hearing "immediately" our earth produces grass, and this grass, before it comes to maturity or to fruit, "withers," our earth will be called "rocky." But if the things that are said rest on deeper roots in our heart, so that they both "bear fruit" of works and have in themselves the seeds of future ones, then truly the earth of each one of us bears fruit according to its power, one "a hundredfold," another "sixtyfold," another "thirtyfold." But we have thought it necessary to give this warning also, that our fruit nowhere have "tares," that is, nowhere have "darnel," so that it may not be "along the way," but may be sown in the very way, in that which says: "I am the way," so that "the birds of heaven" may not eat our fruits nor our vineyard.

Three classes of men are introduced as enquiring of John concerning their salvation, one which the Scripture calls the multitude, another to which it gives the name of Publicans, and a third which is noticed by the appellation of soldiers.

But this place admits of a deeper meaning, for as we ought not to serve two masters, so neither to have two coats, lest one should be the clothing of the old man, the other of the new, but we ought to cast off the old man, and give to him who is naked. For one man has one coat, another has none at all, the strength therefore of the two is exactly contrary, and as it has been written that we should cast all our crimes to the bottom of the sea, so ought we to throw from us our vices and errors, and lay them upon him who has been the cause of them.

And that this may become clearer, let me set down the parable of the minas. He who had received one mina and had made ten and offered it to the Lord, by whom the mina had been entrusted to him, received also another which he had not had before. For the mina of him who had not multiplied what he had received the Lord orders to be taken away and given to the one who has others; "take away", he says, "the mina and give it to him who has ten minas". And in this manner, the things we have given to God he will restore to us, those very things, together with the things we had not had before. God exacts and requires of us, so that he may have occasion for giving, so that he himself may bestow, who paid it out. For by his own grace the mina was doubled, and to each of the worthy more was given than they hoped for.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 39

quotes.quote: This journey, then, must be made by those who follow God; but there is also a tower on this journey. What is that tower? That one, surely, of which the Lord says in the Gospel: "which of you, wishing to build a tower, will not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has the means to complete it?" This, then, is the tower, the steep and lofty seat of the virtues.

Or in another way; Frequently are men delivered from the hands of the enemy, but not without fear. For when fear and peril have gone before, and a man is then plucked from the enemies' hand, he is delivered indeed, but not without fear. Therefore said he, that the coming of Christ caused us to be snatched from the enemies' hands without fear. For we suffered not from their evil designs, but He suddenly parting us from them, hath led us out to our own allotted resting place.

Or, a way must be prepared in our heart for the Lord, for the heart of man is large and spacious if it has become clean. For imagine not that in the size of the body, but in the virtue of the understanding, consists that greatness which must receive the knowledge of the truth. Prepare then in thy heart by good conversation a way for the Lord, and by perfect works pursue the path of life, that so the word of God may have free course in thee.

But this very thing, which is now set down from the old instrument, we read written in the prophet Isaiah. For there it is said: "The voice of one crying in the desert: prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight". The Lord wishes to find ways in you—he who, that he may be able to enter into your souls and make his journey, prepare for him the path of which it is said: "make his paths straight". "The voice of one crying in the desert". "The voice" cries: "prepare the way"; for first "the voice" reaches the ears, then after the voice—rather, together with the voice—the word penetrates the hearing. According to this sense Christ was announced by John. Let us see, therefore, what "the voice" announces concerning the word. "Prepare", it says, "the way for the Lord". What "way for the Lord" are we to prepare? Surely not a bodily one? Or can the word of God travel by such a road? Or…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 21

quotes.quote: Then "he came into Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and having entered according to his custom into the synagogue on the sabbath day, he stood up to read; and the book of the prophet Isaiah was given to him; and unrolling the book he found the place where it was written: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; wherefore he has anointed me". Not by chance did he unroll the book and find the chapter prophesying about himself as the reading, but this too was of the providence of God. For just as it is written: "A sparrow does not fall into the snare without the will of the Father", and because "the hairs of the head" of the apostles "are all numbered", so perhaps this also — that the book of Isaiah especially was found, and the reading not another, but this one, which spoke the mystery of Christ: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; wherefore he has anointed me" — for it is Christ who…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 32

quotes.quote: Then, moreover, the Savior too, with the authority of the Lord and King, establishing laws and ordinances at once for priests and for the peoples, says: "Take heed, lest perhaps your hearts be weighed down with drunkenness and surfeiting and with the cares of this world, and that sudden destruction come upon you". You have heard the edict of the eternal King, and you have learned the lamentable end of "drunkenness" or "surfeiting". If some skilled and wise physician were to prescribe to you in these very words and say: Take heed to yourselves, lest anyone, for example's sake, take too greedily of the juice of this or that herb; for if he does so, sudden destruction will come upon him—I do not doubt that everyone, with regard to his own health, would keep the precepts of the physician who forewarned him. But now the physician of souls and bodies, and at the same time the Lord, bids the…
But Jesus is tempted by the devil forty days, and what the temptations were we know not. They were perhaps omitted, as being greater than could be committed to writing.

For it is written: "And he was led into the desert by the Spirit for forty days and was tempted by the devil". For forty days Jesus is tempted, and what the temptations were, we do not know; and these were perhaps passed over for the reason that they were too great to be entrusted to writing. And if it is right to say it thus: just as "the world could not contain all the books", if the things which Jesus taught and did had been written down, so the world could not bear the temptations of the forty days, by which the Lord was tempted by the devil, if Scripture had recorded them. It suffices for us to know only this much: that "he was for forty days in the desert and was tempted by the devil and ate nothing in those days"; for he was mortifying the sense of the flesh by continual and unbroken fasting.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 29

quotes.quote: Both of the things that are said and of those that are reported as done, the account ought to be worthy of the Holy Spirit and of the faith of Christ, to which we who believe are called. Hence now too the reason must be sought why Mary, after her conceiving, came to Elizabeth and "remained with her three months"; or what the reason was that Luke, who was writing the history of the Gospel, should also insert this, that she "remained with her three months, and afterwards returned to her own house". Surely there ought to be some reason which, if the Lord opens our heart, the discourse that follows will show. For if from the mere fact that Mary came to Elizabeth and greeted her, "the infant leaped for joy", and "Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit", prophesied those things which are written in the Gospel, and in a single hour made such great advances, it is left to our conjecture how…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 9

quotes.quote: The officer does not have the power to be able to remit to me even a "farthing" and the smallest portion; there is one who can remit to debtors who have nothing wherewith to pay. "There approached him", he says, "one who owed five hundred denarii, and another fifty; and since they had nothing wherewith to pay, he forgave them both". He who forgave was the master; but this one, who is the officer, is not the master, but is appointed by the master to exact the debts. You were not worthy that five hundred or fifty denarii should be forgiven you, nor did you deserve to hear: "your offenses are forgiven you".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 35

quotes.quote: And, to come to the things that are written, the "Lord of majesty", Jesus Christ our Savior, was crucified. The author of this crime and the father of the wickedness is without doubt the devil. For thus it is written: "but when the devil had entered into the heart of Judas Iscariot, that he should betray him". The father of the sin, then, is the devil. He, in this wickedness, first begets a son, Judas; but Judas alone could not accomplish this. What, then, is written? "Judas went" it says "to the scribes and Pharisees and to the chief priests, saying to them: What will you give me, and I will betray him to you?" There is born, then, from Judas a third and fourth generation of sin. And you will be able to detect this order in each single sin as well.

As far as Luke's narrative is concerned, our Lord is not yet said to have worked any miracle in Capernaum. For before He came to Capernaum, He is said to have lived at Nazareth. I cannot but think therefore that in these words, "whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum," there lies a mystery concealed, and that Nazareth is a type of the Jews, Capernaum of the Gentiles. For the time will come when the people of Israel shall say, "The things which thou hast shown to the whole world, show also to us." Preach thy word to the people of Israel, that then at least, when the fulness of the Gentiles has entered, all Israel may be saved. Our Saviour seems to me to have well answered, No prophet is accepted in his own country, but rather according to the type than the letter; though neither was Jeremiah accepted in Anathoth his country, nor the rest of the Prophets. But it seems rather to be…

See then the greatness of the Saviour, how it is diffused over the whole world. Go up to heaven, see there how it has filled the heavenly places; carry thy thoughts down to the deep, behold, there too He has descended. If thou seest this, then, in like manner, beholdest thou fulfilled in very deed, He shall be great.

On account of this the angel says to her: "fear not, Mary! for you have found grace before the Lord. Behold, you shall conceive in your womb, and you shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. He shall be great and shall be called the Son of the Most High". Of John also it is said, "he shall be great", and Gabriel the angel testifies to this very thing; but when Jesus came, truly great, truly exalted, he who before had been "great" was made lesser. For "he", he says, "was a burning and shining lamp, and you were willing for a while to rejoice in his light". The greatness of our Savior did not appear then, when he was born, but now — after he seemed to be crushed by his adversaries — it has shone forth.

See the greatness of the Lord: "into all the earth has the sound of his teaching gone out, and his words unto the ends of the world". Our Lord Jesus, because he is the power of…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 6

quotes.quote: Now if the Lord could neither receive increase or decrease, what is this that Mary speaks of, My soul doth magnify (magnificat) the Lord? But if I consider that the Lord our Saviour is the image of the invisible God, and that the soul is created according to His image, so as to be an image of an image, then I shall see plainly, that as after the manner of those who are accustomed to paint images, each one of us forming his soul after the image of Christ, makes it great or little, base or noble, after the likeness of the original; so when I have made my soul great in thought, word, and deed, the image of God is made great, and the Lord Himself, whose image it is, is magnified in my soul.

For He gives the name of the eye especially to our understanding, but the whole soul, although not corporeal, He metaphorically calls the body. For the whole soul is enlightened by the understanding.

For the understanding from its very beginning desires only singleness, containing no dissimulation, or guile, or division in itself.
But the soul first magnifies the Lord, that it may afterwards rejoice in God; for unless we have first believed, we can not rejoice.

By wiping off the dust of their feet against them, they in some sort say, The dust of your sins shall deservedly come upon you. And mark that the cities which receive not the Apostles and sound doctrine have streets, according to Matthew, Broad is the way which leadeth to destruction. (Matt. 7:13.)

Answering them, the Savior said: "You are in error, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection of the dead they will neither marry nor be given in marriage, but they will be like the angels in heaven". Those who will be like the angels will certainly be angels. And at the same time it must be learned that the angels have no marriages. Here indeed, where there is death, both marriages and children are necessary; but where there is immortality, there is need neither of wedlock nor of sons. Let me set before myself a very troublesome question, one that is not easily solved, in the person of those who are most zealous for the Scriptures and who "meditate day and night in the law of the Lord". Where, they say, is it written that "they will neither marry nor be given in marriage"? Passing through both the Old and the New Testament in memory and mind, I do not…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 39

quotes.quote: But if you wish also through examples to know how each one is bowed down by his sins, so that he cannot look up nor lift his eyes to heaven, gaze upon that publican who in the Gospel, having entered the temple and standing afar off, not daring to lift his eyes to heaven, but striking his breast and confessing his sins, said: "God, be merciful to me a sinner." To this man surely it is fitting to say, "I am bowed down even to the end, and I went about all the day saddened." And in saying this, he sets forth, as it were, the very disposition and soul of the penitent, who says: From the time I sinned, I have never laughed, I have never been glad, I have never indulged myself in anything of enjoyment, but I have always been in mourning, always in repentance, always in grief.

But because the Lord was baptized and the heavens were opened and "the Holy Spirit descended" upon him and a voice thundered from the heavens saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased", it must be said that at the baptism of Jesus heaven was unbarred, and that the heavens were opened for the dispensation of the remission of sins—not of him "who had done no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth"—but for the whole world.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 27

quotes.quote: But the same cure which the woman obtained by touching Him, our Saviour confirmed by His word; as it follows, And he said unto her, Thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, that is, Be released from thy scourge. And indeed He first heals her soul by faith, then truly her body.
He who has bought five yoke of oxen is he who neglects his intellectual nature, and follows the things of sense, therefore he cannot comprehend a spiritual nature.

Having related our Lord's baptism, he next enters upon the generation of the Lord, not bringing it down from the higher to the lower, but beginning with Christ, he carries it up to God Himself. Hence he says, And Jesus Himself began. For when He was baptized, and had Himself undergone the mystery of the second birth, then He is said to have begun, that thou also mightest destroy this first birth and be born in the second.

The Lord descending into the world took upon Him the person of all sinners, and was willing to be born of the stock of Solomon, (as Matthew relates,) whose sins have been written down, and of the rest, many of whom did evil in the sight of God. But when He ascended, and is described as being born a second time in baptism, (as Luke relates,) He is not born through Salomon, but Nathan, who reproves the father for the death of Uriah, and the birth of Solomon.

Our Lord and Savior, who was far better than Melchizedek, whose lineage Scripture has not disclosed, is now described as having been born according to the order of the fathers; and although his divinity is not subject to any human beginning, for your sake, who were born in the flesh, he willed to be born. And yet the order of his birth is not narrated in the same way by the evangelists, a matter which has greatly troubled some people. For Matthew, beginning to weave the sequence of that birth from Abraham, arrives at the point of saying: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was in this way", and he describes not the one who was baptized, but the one who came into the world; whereas Luke, in setting forth his birth, does not lead down from higher to lower, but, when he had first spoken of him as baptized, ascends all the way to God himself. Nor are the persons the same in his genealogy when he…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 28

quotes.quote: For he who "went out to sow" "sows the word" over every place, but hear the Lord himself saying what the seed of God is wont to suffer: "some," he says, "fell by the wayside, and the birds of heaven come and snatch it away." Which, interpreting in what follows, he himself says: "but those who were sown by the wayside are they who hear the word of God and receive it with joy; but the devil comes and takes away from their heart what was sown." So therefore these too now come to the seed of God and wish to "take it away from the heart of those in whom it was sown," because they find them placed in the valleys and pursuing all that is lowest. For they belong to those who receive the word of God humbly and unworthily and, so to speak, with a Jewish understanding, and therefore the demons are able to "snatch it away from their heart." But he who ascends from the humility of the letter to the…

But that He blessed them with uplifted hands, signifies that it becomes him who blesses any one to be furnished with various works and labours in behalf of others. For in this way are the hands raised up on high.

When a father is asked by his son for bread, he does not give him a stone for bread, but the devil like a crafty and deceitful foe gives stones for bread.

I suppose also that even now at this very time the devil shows a stone to men that he may tempt them to speak, saying to them, Command this stone to be made bread. If thou seest the heretics devouring their lying doctrines as if they were bread, know that their teaching is a stone which the devil shows them.

"And when the days were completed, he hungered. And the devil said to him: If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread". "Tell", he says, "this stone". Which stone? Surely the one the devil was pointing out, the one he wants to be made bread. What sort of temptation is this, that when a son asks his father for bread and the father does not give him a stone, this adversary, crafty and deceitful, should give a stone in place of bread? Is this the whole of what the devil wanted — that a stone should become bread, and that men should feed not on bread but on a stone, which the devil had pointed out in place of bread? I think that even to this day the devil shows a stone and urges each person to say: "tell this stone to become bread". By every temptation with which men were to be tempted, the Lord was tempted first, according to his assumption of the flesh. And he is tempted…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 29

quotes.quote:
In the spirit and power of Elijah.—He says not, in the mind of Elijah, but in the spirit and power. For the spirit which was in Elijah came upon John, and in like manner his power.

This sacrament of preparation is even now fulfilled in the world, for even now the spirit and power of John must come upon the soul, before it believes in Jesus Christ.

"And he shall go before Christ in the spirit and power of Elijah". He does not say: in the soul of Elijah, but: "in the spirit and power of Elijah". There was in Elijah a power and a spirit, as in all the prophets, and, according to the dispensation of the body, in the Lord and Savior himself also, of whom a little later it is said to Mary: "the Holy Spirit shall come upon you and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you". The spirit, therefore, which had been in Elijah, came into John, and the power which was in him appeared in this one also. The former was translated, but the latter was the forerunner of the Lord and died before him, so that, descending also to the lower regions, he might there proclaim his coming.

I think that the mystery of John is fulfilled in the world down to this very day. Whoever is to believe in Christ Jesus, first the spirit and power of John comes to…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 4

quotes.quote:
As we have died with Him at His death, and risen together with Him at His resurrection, so with Him have we been circumcised, and therefore need not now circumcision in the flesh.

But the name of Jesus, a glorious name and worthy of all honour, a name which is above every other, ought not first to be uttered by men, nor by them be brought into the world. Therefore significantly the Evangelist adds, which was called of the Angel, &c.

In "that he died," Christ "died to sin"; not because he himself had sinned — "for he did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" — but he died so that we, who were dead, might, by his dying "to sins," by no means live "to sin" and to vices. Whence it is written: "If we have died together with him, we shall also live together with him"; therefore, just as "we died together" then, when he died, and rose together with him when he rose again, so were we circumcised with him and, after the circumcision, cleansed by the solemn purification. Whence we now have no need whatsoever of carnal circumcision. And that you may know that he was circumcised for our sake, hear Paul preaching most plainly: "in whom," he says, "dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily, and you are filled in him, who is the head of all principality and power; in whom also you were circumcised with a circumcision…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 14

quotes.quote: For it is not by incantations that Christians seem to prevail (over evil spirits), but by the name of Jesus, accompanied by the announcement of the narratives which relate to Him; for the repetition of these has frequently been the means of driving demons out of men, especially when those who repeated them did so in a sound and genuinely believing spirit. Such power, indeed, does the name of Jesus possess over evil spirits, that there have been instances where it was effectual, when it was pronounced even by bad men, which Jesus Himself taught (would be the case), when He said: "Many shall say to Me in that day, In Thy name we have cast out devils, and done many wonderful works." Whether Celsus omitted this from intentional malignity, or from ignorance, I do not know.

Furthermore, since something was added about the image of Caesar, we must also touch briefly upon this. Some suppose that it was said by the Savior simply: "render to Caesar what is Caesar's", that is: pay the tribute which you owe. For who among us objects to paying tribute to Caesar? Therefore the passage holds something mystical and hidden. There are two images in man: one, which he received from God when he was made in the beginning, as it is written in Genesis: "according to the image and likeness of God"; the other of the earthy, which afterward, when he had been cast out of paradise because of disobedience and sin, he took on, persuaded by the enticements of "the prince of this world". For just as a coin or denarius bears the image of the emperors of the world, so he who does the works of "the ruler of these darknesses" bears the image of him whose works he has: which image Jesus…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 39

quotes.quote: If the completion of all things had been then already begun, and the end of time close at hand, I should have no question but that the prophecy was given, because at that time it was to be fulfilled. But now that many ages have elapsed since the Spirit spoke this, I think it was prophesied to the people of Israel, because their cutting off was approaching. For to those that went out to him that they should be baptized, he gave this warning among others.

John at that time was already speaking: "Behold, the axe is laid to the root of the trees". And indeed, if the consummation were already pressing in and the end of the times were at hand, no question would arise for me. For I would say that what he says—"Behold, the axe is laid to the root of the trees"—and that other saying—"Every tree, therefore, that does not bear good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire"—was prophesied for this reason, because it was being fulfilled at that time. But since so many ages have flowed by since then, and such innumerable years have passed from that time to the present day, we must inquire how the Holy Spirit says in the prophet: "Behold, the axe is laid to the root of the trees". I think it is prophesied to the people of Israel, that their cutting-down is near. For "to those" who "were going out" to him, "to be baptized", he was saying, among…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 23

quotes.quote: Learn where those seeking him find him, so that you too, seeking with Joseph and Mary, may find him. And seeking him, it says, "they found him in the temple". Not anywhere in some other place, but "in the temple", and not simply "in the temple", but "in the midst of the teachers, hearing them and questioning them". You too, therefore, seek Jesus "in the temple" of God, seek him in the Church, seek him among the masters who are "in the temple" and do not go out from it; for if you seek in this way, you will find him. Moreover, if anyone says that he is a master and does not have Jesus, that man is a master in name only, and therefore Jesus, the word of God and wisdom, cannot be found with him. He was found, it says, "in the midst of the teachers". Just as it is written in another place concerning the prophets, so also now understand "in the midst of the teachers". "If", it says,…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 18

quotes.quote: Where, then, do they find him? "In the temple"; for there the Son of God is found. If ever you too shall seek the Son of God, seek first the temple, hasten thither, there you will find Christ, the Word and the wisdom, that is, the Son of God. But because he was a little one, he is found "in the midst of the teachers", sanctifying and instructing them. Because he was a little one, he is found "in the midst" not teaching them, but "questioning", and this in accordance with the duty of his age, that he might teach us what befits children, however wise and learned they be, namely that they should rather hear their masters than desire to teach, and should not vaunt themselves with vain display. He was questioning, I say, the masters, not that he might learn something, but that in questioning he might instruct. For from one fountain of teaching flows both to question and to answer wisely; and…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 19

quotes.quote: "And it came to pass", he says, "when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another: Let us go over as far as Bethlehem, and let us see this word that has come to pass, which the Lord has shown to us. And they came in haste, and found Mary and Joseph and the child". Because they had come in haste, and not step by step nor with weary tread, therefore they found Joseph the steward of the Lord's birth, and Mary who brought forth Jesus in childbirth, and the Savior himself "lying in a manger". That was the manger of which the prophet prophesied, saying: "the ox knew its owner, and the ass the manger of its lord". The ox is a clean animal, the ass an unclean animal. "The ass knew the manger of its lord". It was not the people of Israel who knew the manger of their lord, but an unclean animal from among the Gentiles: "but Israel", he says, "has not known me,…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 13

quotes.quote: Of old "the word of God came to Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, who was of the priests" in the time of this or that king of Judah; now "the word of God comes to John, the son of Zechariah", which never came to the prophets "in the desert". But because "the children" of the desolate one "were to be more" than of "her who has a husband", therefore "the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the desert". And at the same time consider that it has more reason in it, if the desert is understood mystically and not according to the simple letter. For he who preaches "in the desert" acts to no purpose in crying out there where no one hears him speaking. The forerunner of Christ, therefore, and "the voice of one crying in the desert", preaches "in the desert" of the soul that does not have peace. And not only then, but also in the present, first "the burning and shining lamp" comes and…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 21

quotes.quote: If any then sells, let him be cast out, and especially if he sells doves. For of those things which have been revealed and committed to me by the Holy Spirit, I either sell for money to the people, or do not teach without hire, what else do I but sell a dove, that is, the Holy Spirit?

After this it is said: "he entered into the temple", and, when he had entered, "he cast out those who were selling doves". He did not cast out those who buy; for he who buys, possesses what he has bought. Those Jesus cast out of his Father's temple who sell and throw away what they had, after the likeness of that prodigal son who received his substance from his father and lost it all in excessive drinking. If, therefore, anyone sells, he is cast out, especially if he was selling "doves". Why did he name no other birds but doves? This animal is simple and comely. I fear lest this same fault be found in us also. For if the things that have been revealed and entrusted to me by the Holy Spirit, that I might bring them forth to the multitude, I should sell for a price and not teach without wage, what else do I do but sell doves, that is, the Holy Spirit? And when I have sold him, I am cast…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 38

quotes.quote: I beg you to remember in your entire present contest the great reward laid up in heaven for those who are persecuted and reviled for righteousness' sake. Be glad and leap for joy on account of the Son of man, just as the apostles once rejoiced when they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for his name.

My Lord Jesus was born, and his parents went up to Jerusalem to fulfill the things that had been commanded in the law, and to offer for him "a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons". Simeon held him in his arms, as was read a little while ago, and prophesied concerning him the things that the account relates. And after everything was completed according to custom, the parents returned. In what year was Jesus at that time? He was assuredly still a little child, and yet he "grew and became strong and was filled with wisdom" and grace; he had not yet completed the forty days of purification, he had not yet come to Nazareth, and already he was receiving all wisdom. Scripture could have said: "he grew and became strong, and received the Spirit"; but because "he had emptied himself, taking the form of a servant", as soon as the sacrifice was offered for his purification, that which he had…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 18

quotes.quote: Since some who seem to believe the holy Scriptures deny the divinity of the Savior, as though for the glory of the almighty God, it seems just to me that they should be taught from the authority of those very Scriptures that something divine came into a human body, and not only into a human body, but also into a human soul. Yet, if we attend carefully to the meaning of the Scriptures, that soul had something more than the rest of human souls. For every human soul, before it comes to virtue, is defiled by vices. But the soul of Jesus was never stained with the filth of sin. Indeed, before he reached the twelfth year of his age, the Holy Spirit writes concerning him in the Gospel of Luke: "But the boy grew and was strengthened and was filled with wisdom". This human nature does not admit, that one should be filled with wisdom before twelve years. It is one thing to have a part of wisdom,…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 19

quotes.quote: (in Matt. tom. 13.) But it is not clearly expressed by whom He is to be delivered, for one says, that He is to be delivered up by Judas, another by the devil; but Paul says, that God the Father delivered Him up for us all; (Rom. 8:32.) but Judas, as he delivered Him up for money, did it traitorously, the Father for His mercies' sake.

A new face suddenly presenting itself to the human eye, troubles and startles the mind. The angel knowing this to be the nature of man, first dispels the alarm, as it follows, But the angel said unto him, Fear not.

The angel not only soothes his fears, but gladdens him with good tidings, adding, For thy prayer is heard, and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear a son.

Or they knew not whether when He said about my Father's business, He referred to the temple, or something higher and more edifying; for every one of us who doeth good, is the seat of God the Father; but whoso is the seat of God the Father, has Christ in the midst of him.

Jordan is the same as descending, for there descends from God a river of healing water. But what parts would John be traversing but the country lying about Jordan, that the penitent sinner might soon arrive at the flowing stream, humbling himself to receive the baptism of repentance. For it is added, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.

And "he came into all the country round about the Jordan". For what other places ought the Baptist to have gone around, except those neighboring the Jordan, so that whoever wished to do penance might be at hand for the washing of water? Moreover, "Jordan" is interpreted "descending". And the river "descending" and running with a great rush is God our Savior, the Lord, into whom we are baptized with true water, with saving water. Baptism is preached also "for the remission of sins": Come, catechumens, do penance, that you may obtain baptism "for the remission" of sins. He receives baptism "for the remission of sins" who ceases to sin. For if anyone comes to the washing while sinning, no remission of sins is made for him. Therefore I beseech you, do not come to baptism without caution and careful circumspection, but first show "fruits worthy of repentance"! Spend some time in good…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 21

quotes.quote: According to which sense our Lord and Savior too, since he is "spirit", "came to send fire upon the earth"; "spirit" according to that which is written: "but when you have turned to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away", and: "the Lord is a spirit". But "he came to send fire" not upon heaven, but "upon the earth", as he himself shows when he says: "I came to send fire upon the earth, and what do I wish but that it already blaze?" For if "you have turned to the Lord", who is "spirit", Christ will be "spirit" to you and "he did not come to send fire upon the earth". But if you are not turned to him, but have earth and its fruits, "he came to send fire upon" your "earth".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 26

quotes.quote: He followed evidently as a wrestler, gladly setting out to meet the temptation, and saying, as it were, Lead me where you will, and you will find me the stronger in every thing.

Search the Scriptures, so that even in those things which are thought to be simple you may discover mysteries that are by no means small. Let us search the beginning of the Gospel reading which we have heard today, and let what was hidden come forth into the open. "He brought," it says, that is, the devil brought Jesus "into Jerusalem." This is incredible, that the devil should lead the Son of God and that he should follow. Yet he clearly followed, like an athlete going of his own accord to the contest. He did not dread the tempter, nor was he afraid of the snares of the craftiest of enemies, and in a certain manner he was saying: lead where you wish, tempt as you please, of my own accord I give myself over to be tempted, I endure whatever you may suggest, I offer myself in whatever you may try: you will find me stronger in all things. "He brought him therefore into Jerusalem, and set…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 31

quotes.quote: They who have bought a piece of ground and reject or refuse the supper, are they who have taken other doctrines of divinity, but have despised the word which they possessed.

Although there are many precepts in the law, the Savior set down in the Gospel only these, which by a kind of summary would lead the obedient to eternal life. For he has regard to that which the doctor of the law had asked him, saying: "Master, what shall I do to possess eternal life?" — the reading which according to Luke has today been recited to you. He answered: "What is written in the law? how do you read? You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole strength, and with your whole mind; and your neighbor as yourself". And then he said: "You have answered well; do this, and you shall live". There is no doubt that it is everlasting life about which both the doctor of the law had inquired and the Savior's discourse had treated. And at the same time we are plainly taught that it is commanded in the law that we should love God. In…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 34

quotes.quote: The "infant", then, "leaped in the womb of Elizabeth, and she was filled with the Holy Spirit and cried out with a loud voice and said: Blessed art thou among women". In this place we must, lest any of the simple be deceived, refute the objections that heretics are accustomed to raise. For a certain man—I know not who—broke out into such madness as to assert that Mary was disowned by the Savior, on the ground that after His birth she was joined to Joseph; and he spoke words which, with what sort of mind he uttered them, he himself who spoke them knows. If therefore heretics should ever bring some such objection against you, answer them and say: Surely Elizabeth, full "of the Holy Spirit", says: "blessed art thou among women". If Mary is proclaimed blessed by the Holy Spirit, how did the Savior disown her? Furthermore, as for their assertion that she married after the birth, they have no…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 7

quotes.quote:
If we marvel to hear that a woman was healed by touching the hem of a garment, what must we think of Simeon, who received an Infant in his arms, and rejoiced seeing that the little one he carried was He who had come to let loose the captive. Knowing that no one could release him from the chains of the body with the hope of future life, but He whom he held in his arms. Therefore it is said, And he blessed God, saying, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart.

As if he said, "As long as I held not Christ, I was in prison, and could not escape from my bonds."

It is plain that of one kind of knowledge, the end is in the knowledge itself, as in geometry; but of another kind, the end is counted to be in the work, as in medicine; and so it is in the word of God, and therefore having signified the knowledge by the words were themselves eyewitnesses, he points out the work by what follows, and were ministers of the word.

It is written in Exodus, The people saw the voice of the Lord. (Exod. 20:18.) Now a voice is rather heard than seen. But it was so written, to show us that men see the voice of the Lord with other eyes, which they only have who are worthy of them. Again in the Gospel, it is not the voice that is perceived, but the Word, which is more excellent than the voice.

"As they have handed down to us, who from the beginning themselves saw and were ministers of the word". In Exodus it is written: "the people saw the voice of God". And surely a voice is heard rather than seen; but it was written thus for this reason, that it might be shown to us that with other eyes one may "see the voice of God" — those eyes with which they behold who are worthy. Moreover in the Gospel not a voice is perceived, but a word, which is more excellent than a voice. Whence it is now said: "as they have handed down to us, who from the beginning themselves saw and were ministers of the word". Therefore the apostles themselves saw the word, not because they had looked upon the body of the Lord and Savior, but because they had seen the Word. For if to have seen Jesus according to the body is this, namely to have seen the word of God, then Pilate too, who condemned Jesus, saw the…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 1

quotes.quote: (ut sup.) But we should know that they who are taken up with banquetings and worldly cares do not ascend into that upper part of the house, and therefore do not keep the Passover with Jesus. For after the words of the disciples wherewith they questioned the goodman of the house, (that is, the understanding,) the Divine Person came into that house to feast there with His disciples.
And therefore he says, Five months, that is, until Mary should conceive, and her babe leaping with joy should prophesy.

"When Elizabeth conceived, she hid herself for five months, saying: for thus has the Lord done for me in the days in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among men". I ask for what reason, after she understood that she was pregnant, she withdrew from the public eye? Unless I am mistaken, this is the reason: Even those who are joined in marriage do not have every time free for intercourse between themselves, but there is a time when they withdraw from the work of marriage. For if a man be old and a woman aged, it is a matter of the greatest shame for them to be slaves to lust, to be slaves to the conjugal act, when they seem, by the decay of the body and by old age and by the will of God, to have been lifted above such things. But this woman, because at the word of the angel and by the dispensation of God she had again been joined to her husband, was ashamed that, being aged…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 6

quotes.quote: Both the Son of God and the Antichrist have a zeal for reigning. But the Antichrist desires to reign in order to kill those whom he has subjected to himself; Christ reigns for this purpose, that he may save. And each one of us, if he is faithful, is ruled by Christ through the word, wisdom, justice, truth. But if we are lovers of pleasure more than lovers of God, we are ruled by sin, concerning which the Apostle speaks: "let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body". Two kings, therefore, hasten in rivalry to reign: the king of sin over sinners, the devil; the king of justice over the just, Christ. And the devil, knowing that Christ had come for this purpose, to take away his kingdom, and that those who were under him should begin to be under Christ, "showed him all the kingdoms of the world" and of the men of this age—how some are ruled by fornication, others by avarice, how these…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 30

quotes.quote: He showed the innumerable multitudes of men who were held under his dominion. And in truth, if we are willing simply to confess our misery and unhappiness, the devil is king of almost the whole world; whence too he is called "the prince of this age" by the Savior. What he says, therefore, is this: Do you see these men who are under my kingdom?—and "he showed him in a moment of time", that is, in the present course of the ages, which, in comparison with eternity, holds the place of a point. For the Savior had no need that the affairs of this age should be displayed to him for any length of time: as soon as he turned the keen edge of his eyes to contemplate, he beheld both the sins that reign and those who are ruled by vices, and the very "prince of the age", the devil, exulting and rejoicing to his own ruin, because he held so many under his dominion.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 30

quotes.quote: (Hom. i. in Luc.) The effect upon his own mind, St. Luke explains by the expression, of the things which have been fully accomplished among us, i. e. have had their full manifestation among us, (as the Greek word peplerophoremenon signifies, which the Latin cannot express in one word,) for he had been convinced of them by sure faith and reason, and wavered not in any thing.

Just as of old among the people of the Jews many laid claim to prophecy, and some were false prophets — of whom one was Hananiah, the son of Azor —, while others were true prophets, and there was in the people the grace of discerning spirits, by which some were received among the prophets, while a few were rejected as though by "the most experienced money-changers", so also now, in the new covenant, "many have attempted" to write gospels, but not all have been received. And that you may know that not only four gospels, but very many, have been composed, out of which these that we have were chosen and handed down to the churches, let us learn from the very preface of Luke, which runs thus: "Forasmuch as many have attempted to set in order a narrative". In this that he says, "they have attempted", there lies a hidden accusation of those who, without the grace of the Holy Spirit, leapt…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 1

quotes.quote: (sup. Joan. tom. ii.) Now I think this place is not without reason said to be a small village. For as if it were a village without any further name, in comparison of the whole earth the whole heavenly country is despised.
As long as our Lord was in the mount His Apostles only were with Him, but when He began to be near the descent, then there came to Him a multitude of the people.

Which of us is so blessed that Jesus sits upon him — Jesus, who, as long as he was on the mountain, tarried with the apostles alone, but when he began to be near the descent, then the crowd of peoples met him? If he had not come to the descent, the multitude could not have met him. He came down and sat upon the colt of the donkey, and all the people with one accord praised God.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 37

quotes.quote:
But John, who had commenced his Gospel from God, saying, In the beginning was the Word, did not describe the temptation of the Lord, because God can not be tempted, of whom he wrote. But because in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke the human generations are given, and in Mark it is man who is tempted, therefore Matthew, Luke, and Mark have described the temptation of the Lord.

The Lord having overcome the tempter, power was added to Him, i. e. as far as regards the manifestation of it. Hence it is said, And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit.

First indeed: "Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the desert for forty days". When he was being tempted by the devil, and because he was still to contend against him, once and again "Spirit" is set down without any addition. But when he had overcome by his fighting the three temptations which Scripture records, see what is placed concerning the Spirit pointedly and carefully. "Jesus", it says, "returned in the power of the Spirit". "Power" is added, because he had trampled upon the dragon and had conquered the tempter in close combat. "Jesus" therefore "returned in the power of the Spirit into the land of Galilee, and the report went out concerning him through all the surrounding region."
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 32

quotes.quote: But you too, who hear these things, if you attend to the holy Scriptures in your leisure, will find very many deeds of great matters contained under the number thirty or fifty. At thirty years of age Joseph is brought out of prison and receives the sovereignty of all Egypt, that by divine foresight he might drive off the ruin of the impending famine. Jesus is related to be of thirty years when He came to the baptism and "saw the heavens divided and the Spirit of God coming upon Himself in the likeness of a dove"; where also the mystery of the Trinity first began to be disclosed.

When Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, there came to him a woman having an alabaster jar of precious ointment and poured it upon his head as he reclined. But when his disciples saw it, they were indignant, and so forth (26:6—13).

Many indeed suppose that the four evangelists have given an account of one and the same woman, because they wrote something of this kind about a woman and all alike named an alabaster jar of ointment; but John, instead of the alabaster jar, put "a pound of ointment." But also what is said, this could have been sold and given to the poor, was said by Matthew and Mark and John; and that Christ declared that ointment to have been poured out for his burial, these too expounded; and that it happened in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, these three wrote; but John indeed said Bethany, where "they made him a supper and Martha was serving…

"Now the tax collectors also came to be baptized by him". This, even according to the simple understanding, may teach the tax collectors to seek "nothing more" than what is commanded in the law; for those who exact more transgress not the commandment of John, but of the Holy Spirit, who spoke in John. But I do not know whether, according to the ἀναγωγήν (the anagogical or higher sense), the discourse signifies something else more excellent, and whether we ought to bring forth things so mystical in such an audience, especially among those who do not look into the marrow of the Scriptures, but delight only in the surface. It is indeed dangerous, yet it must be touched upon summarily and briefly. When we have departed from the world and this our life has been changed, there will be certain ones sitting at the boundaries of the world, most diligently searching, as if by the office of tax…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 23

quotes.quote: The holy Virgin knew that He was not the Son of Joseph, and yet calls her husband His father according to the belief of the Jews, who thought that He was conceived in the common way. Now to speak generally we may say, that the Holy Spirit honoured Joseph by the name of father, because he brought up the Child Jesus; but more technically, that it might not seem superfluous in St. Luke, bringing down the genealogy from David to Joseph. But why sought they Him sorrowing? Was it that he might have perished or been lost? It could not be. For what should cause them to dread the loss of Him whom they knew to be the Lord? But as whenever you read the Scriptures you search out their meaning with pains, not that you suppose them to have erred or to contain anything incorrect, but that the truth which they have inherent in them you are anxious to find out; so they sought Jesus, lest perchance…

Therefore, that we too may hear him and that he may set before us questions which he himself may resolve, let us beseech him and seek him with the utmost labor and sorrow, and then we shall be able to find him whom we seek. For it is not written in vain: "I and your father have been seeking you with sorrow". He who seeks Jesus must seek not negligently, not carelessly, not in passing, as some seek and therefore cannot find him. But let us say: "with sorrow we seek you".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 18

quotes.quote: There follows: "sorrowing we were seeking you". I do not think that they sorrowed for this reason, because they supposed the boy had strayed or perished; nor could it happen that Mary, who knew that she had conceived of the Holy Spirit, who had heard both the angel speaking and the shepherds hastening and Simeon prophesying, should fear that she might lose the boy through his wandering off. Remove this opinion especially from Joseph, to whom it had been commanded by the angel that he should take the boy and go to Egypt, who had heard: "do not fear to take Mary your wife; for that which is born in her is of the Holy Spirit". It could never come to pass that he should dread as lost the infant whom he had known to be divine. The sorrow and the seeking of the parents sounds like something other than the simple reader understands. Just as you, if ever you read the Scriptures, seek in them…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 19

quotes.quote: And that he might point out the kind of teaching, the disciple proceeds, as John also taught his disciples. Of whom in truth thou hast told us, that among them that are born of women there had arisen none greater than he. And because thou hast commanded us to seek things that are great and eternal, whence shall we arrive at the knowledge of these but from Thee, our God and Saviour?

I think that one of Jesus' disciples was conscious in himself of human weakness, which falls short of knowing how we ought to pray.… Are we then to conclude that a man who was brought up in the instruction of the law, who heard the words of the prophets and did not fail to attend the synagogue, did not know how to pray until he saw the Lord praying "in a certain place"? It would certainly be foolish to say this. The disciple prayed according to the customs of the Jews, but he saw that he needed better knowledge about the subject of prayer.

Frequently some are freed from the hand of foes, but not "without fear". For when dread and danger have first gone before, and thus one has been rescued from the hand of enemies, he is indeed freed, but not "without fear". But the coming of the Lord Jesus rescued us "from the hand of the enemies without fear". For we did not perceive our enemies nor see them fighting against us, but, while we knew it not, we were suddenly snatched from their jaws and their snares. "In a point and a moment" he transferred us "into the inheritance and the portion of the just", and we have been freed "from the hand of the enemies without fear, that we may serve God in holiness and justice before him all our days".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 10

quotes.quote: By which is implied, that the words uttered by the Saviour inflamed the hearts of the hearers to the love of God.

Do you wish that I show you how from the words of the Holy Spirit fire goes forth and kindles the hearts of believers? Hear David saying in the psalm: "the word of the Lord set him on fire". And again it is written in the Gospel, after the Lord had spoken to Cleopas: "was not our heart" it says "burning within us, when he opened to us the Scriptures?". Whence therefore will you burn? Whence will "coals of fire" be found in you, who are never set on fire by the word of the Lord, never inflamed by the words of the Holy Spirit? Hear also elsewhere David himself saying: "my heart grew warm within me, and in my meditation a fire blazes forth".

Whence it is shown that we must not only apply zeal to learning the sacred letters, but must also entreat the Lord and "day and night" beseech him, that the Lamb "from the tribe of Judah" may come and himself, taking the "sealed book," may deign to open it. For he it is who, "opening the Scriptures," kindled the hearts of the disciples, so that they said: "was not our heart burning within us, when he opened to us the Scriptures?"
But we must not wonder that they are called His parents, seeing the one from her childbirth, the other from his knowledge of it, deserved the names of father and mother.

And he wept over Jerusalem, "saying: if you too had known, even in this your day, the things that are for your peace; but now they are hidden from your eyes", and the rest, up to the place where it says: "because you have not known the time of your visitation". Let one of the hearers say: What is said here is plain, and has been fulfilled in deed concerning Jerusalem: for the Roman army surrounded it and laid it waste even to utter destruction, and the time will come when a stone shall not be left upon a stone upon it. I do not deny that that Jerusalem too was destroyed because of the crimes of its inhabitants; but I ask whether perhaps this weeping pertains also to this our Jerusalem. For we are the Jerusalem that is wept over, we who seem to ourselves to have the greater vision. For if, after the mysteries of truth, after the word of the Gospel, after the teaching of the Church and…

quotes.quote: (in Matt. 26:18.) But I think that the man who meets the disciples as they enter into the city, carrying a pitcher of water, was some servant of a master of a house, carrying water in an earthen vessel either for washing or for drinking. And this I think is Moses conveying the spiritual doctrine in fleshly histories. But they who follow him not, do not celebrate the Passover with Jesus.

But I think that the man who, as the disciples entered the city, met them "carrying a jar of water", whom Jesus willed that his disciples should follow as he went into the house, who was bringing that subtle water to the house, so that it might not only be cleansed, but also more fully washed with waters, was a certain one ministering to the householder (that is, to the understanding), carrying cleansing water in an earthen vessel, "that the sublimity of power may be of God", or certainly he was supplying drinkable water in that earthen vessel, so that the Son of God indeed might furnish the produce of the vine, but that understanding, the minister, might furnish out of the law and the prophets the water that is mingled with the wine of the Gospel word. We therefore who desire to be of the Church, wishing to celebrate the Passover with Jesus, let us follow that man who carries a vessel…

And we speak thus not only of the present time, but also of the future. When we shall have passed from the world, God will not appear unto all men, nor will the angels, but unto him only who has a clean heart. The place will neither hinder nor serve any one.

Concerning what is written: "an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense".

Things that are corporeal and lacking in sense-perception, so as to be seen by another, contribute nothing of themselves, but only the eye of another, intent upon them—whether they will it or not—sees them, wherever it has directed its gaze and contemplation. For what can a man, or any other thing surrounded by a gross body, do, when it is present, to keep from being perceived? On the contrary, those things which are heavenly and divine, even when they are present, are not seen unless they themselves will it; and it lies in their will to be seen or not to be seen. It was the grace of God that He appeared to Abraham or to the rest of the prophets—not because the eye of Abraham's heart alone was the cause of his beholding God, but because the grace of God freely offered…
