quotes.quote: Then three orders are introduced of those inquiring of John concerning their salvation: one, which Scripture called "the peoples going out to the baptism"; another, which it names "tax collectors"; a third, which is reckoned under the appellation of "soldiers". "The crowds asked him, saying: What shall we do? And he answering said to them: He who has two tunics, let him give to him who has none, and he who has food, let him do likewise"—which indeed I do not know whether it is fitting to be commanded to the crowds. For it befits the apostles rather than the common people that he who has two tunics should give one to him who has none. And that you may know that this befits the apostles rather than the peoples, hear what is said by the Savior to them: "Do not take two tunics on the way". And so the double garment with which each one is clothed, and the command that he give the other "to…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 23

quotes.quote: When therefore you read that Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit, and it is written in the Acts concerning the Apostles, that they were filled with the Holy Spirit, you must not suppose that the Apostles were equal to the Saviour. For as if you should say, These vessels are full of wine or oil, you would not thereby affirm them to be equally full, so Jesus and Paul were full of the Holy Spirit, but Paul's vessel was far less than that of Jesus, and yet each was filled according to its own measure. Having then received baptism, the Saviour, being full of the Holy Spirit, which came upon Him from heaven in the form of a dove, was led by the Spirit, because, as many as are led by the Spirit, they are the sons of God, (Rom. 8:14.) but He was above all, especially the Son of God.

When you read in the Gospel: "But Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned", and in the Acts of the Apostles, where it is written of them that they were "filled" with "the Holy Spirit", take care not to suppose that the apostles were equal to the Savior; rather, understand that Jesus and the apostles and any other of the saints are full of the Holy Spirit according to the measure of their own vessel. Just as, for example, if you wish to say: these vessels are full of wine or oil, you do not thereby indicate that they are full in equal measure — since one can hold a sextarius, another an urn, another an amphora — in the same way both Jesus and Paul were full of the Holy Spirit; but the vessel of Paul was much smaller than the vessel of Jesus, and yet each was full according to its own measure. And so, having received baptism, the Savior, "full of the Holy Spirit", which had come upon him…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 29

quotes.quote: But who departs from this world in peace, but he who is persuaded that God was Christ reconciling the world to Himself, (2 Cor. 5.) who has nothing hostile to God, having derived to himself all peace by good works in himself?

In my view, and according to the word of God, the soul, released from labors, released from sweats, has been deprived of the flesh and can say: "Now Thou lettest Thy servant depart, O Master, according to Thy word, in peace." It goes forth in peace and reposes with Christ.

Let us inquire into what is written in Luke, the Lord saying: "because it cannot be that a prophet perish outside Jerusalem." If, then, "it cannot be that a prophet perish outside Jerusalem," that is, be killed, you will ask whether after the destruction of Jerusalem there is now no prophet, lest perhaps the one who is killed "outside Jerusalem" should, being a prophet, prove the word of Christ false. But if the scriptures compel us — on account of Agabus and the daughters of Philip the evangelist (not on account of the false prophets of Phrygia) — let us inquire whether perhaps every righteous person is in Jerusalem and not "outside Jerusalem," since "it cannot be" that the one who is outside Jerusalem be afflicted with sufferings for the sake of the word.

But that Jerusalem which is free from the servitude of sin, which is above in its manner of life, "which is our mother," does not…

For of this matter there is also that image which is spoken of in the Gospel concerning "the steward of iniquity," who says to each debtor: "Take your bond, and sitting down write eighty," and the rest that is reported. You see, then, that it is said to each: "Take your bond." Whence it is established that the letters of sin are ours; but the letters of righteousness God writes. For thus says the Apostle: "For you are an epistle inscribed not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone, but on the fleshly tablets of the heart." You have, then, within you the letters of God and the letters of the Holy Spirit. But if you offend, you yourself write for yourself the handwriting of sin. But see that, once you have come to the cross of Christ and to the grace of baptism, your handwriting has been fastened to the cross and blotted out in the font of baptism. Do not…

And when we have said this, he will answer our laboring soul that seeks him with sorrow, and will say: "Do you not know that I must be in my Father's house?". Where are the heretics, where are the impious and the mad, who assert that the law and the prophets do not belong to the Father of Jesus Christ? Surely Jesus was "in the temple" that was built by Solomon, and he confesses that that temple belongs to his Father, whom he revealed to us, whose Son he said he was. Let them answer, how one God is good and another just. Since, therefore, the Savior is the Son of the Creator, let us together praise the Father and the Son, whose is the law, whose also is the temple: to whom be glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 18

quotes.quote: For a feeling of deficiency is the preparation for coming perfection. For whoever by the presence of the apparent good perceives not that he is destitute of the true good, is deprived of the true good.

Or they knew not whether when He said about my Father's business, He referred to the temple, or something higher and more edifying; for every one of us who doeth good, is the seat of God the Father; but whoso is the seat of God the Father, has Christ in the midst of him.

Jesus frequently went down with His disciples, for He is not always dwelling on the mount, for they who were troubled with various diseases were not able to ascend the mount. For this reason now also He went down to them who were below. It follows: And he was subject to them, &c.

Let us then also ourselves be subject to our parents. But if our fathers are not, let us be subject to those who are our fathers. Jesus the Son of God is subject to Joseph and Mary. But I must be subject to the Bishop who has been constituted my father. It seems that Joseph knew that Jesus was greater than he, and therefore in awe moderated…

And at the same time attend to this: that, as long as he was in the possession of his Father, he was above. And because Joseph and Mary did not yet have full faith, for that reason they could not remain above with him, but he is said to have come down with them. Frequently Jesus comes down with his disciples, nor is he always dwelling on the mountain, nor without end does he hold to sublime things. On the mountain he is with Peter, with James, with John, and again in another place with the rest of the disciples. Further, because those who labored under various sicknesses were not able to ascend the mountain, therefore he "came down and came" to those who were below. Now also it is written: "he came down with them and came to Nazareth and was subject to them". Let us learn, children, to be subject to our parents: the greater is subject to the lesser. He, because he saw that Joseph was…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 20

quotes.quote: And at the same time it is shown that this bread, which comes from a stone, is not the word of God which feeds man, of which it is written: "man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word which shall proceed through the mouth of God shall man live". I answer you, O crafty and wicked one, who do not fear to tempt me: there is another bread, that of the word of God, which gives life to man. And at the same time let us see that these things are spoken not by the Son of God, but by the man whom the Son of God deigned to assume; for he answers as though concerning a man and says: "It is written: man shall not live by bread alone", from which it is manifest that it was not God, but man, who was tempted. Sifting the sense of the Scripture diligently, I think I find the reason why John did not describe the temptation of the Lord, but only Matthew, Luke, and Mark. For John, because he had…

quotes.quote: For providence was keeping the half-dead man for him who was stronger than the law and the prophets, namely the Samaritan, which is interpreted "guardian". This is he who "neither slumbers nor sleeps, keeping Israel". On behalf of the half-dead man this Samaritan set out, not going down "from Jerusalem to Jericho" as the priest and the Levite went down; or if he did go down, he went down for this reason, that he might save and guard the one about to die — the Samaritan to whom the Jews said: "You are a Samaritan and have a demon", and who, when he had denied that he had a demon, would not deny that he was a "Samaritan"; for he knew that he was a "guardian". And so when he had come to the half-dead man and had seen him wallowing in his own blood, he took pity and approached him, that he might become his neighbor.

quotes.quote: He cites also another similar example, adding, And there were many lepers in Israel at the time of Eliseus the Prophet, and none of them were cleansed but Naaman the Syrian, who indeed was not of Israel.

But he speaks also another thing pertaining to the same sense: "there were many lepers in Israel in the days of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, except Naaman the Syrian", who assuredly was not of Israel. Consider how up to the present day there are many lepers in "Israel according to the flesh"; see, on the contrary, those drenched with the squalor of leprosy being cleansed by the spiritual Elisha, our Lord and Savior, through the sacrament of baptism, and it being said to you: "rise and go into the Jordan and wash, and your flesh will be restored to you". Naaman rose and went, and having washed he fulfilled the mystery of baptism, "and his flesh became like the flesh of a child". Of what child? Of him who has been born in Christ Jesus "in the washing of regeneration": to whom is glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 33

quotes.quote: As far as Luke's account is concerned, Jesus had not yet stayed in Capernaum, nor is he described as having done any sign there — indeed, in a place where he had not been. But before he came to Capernaum, it is signified that he had been in his own homeland, that is, in Nazareth, and he speaks to his fellow citizens: "You will surely say to me this parable: Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we have heard done in Capernaum, do here also in your own homeland". From this I think that something of a mystery lies hidden in the present passage, and that Nazareth went before as a type of the Jews, Capernaum as a type of the Gentiles. And so Jesus, knowing that he would have no honor in his own homeland — neither he himself, nor the prophets, nor the apostles — was unwilling to preach there, but preached among the Gentiles, lest it be said to him by the men of his own homeland: "You will…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 33

quotes.quote: But if we would rise to a more hidden meaning, I should say, that there were certain shepherd angels, who direct the affairs of men, and while each one of them was keeping his watch, an angel came at the birth of the Lord, and announced to the shepherds that the true Shepherd had arisen. For Angels before the coming of the Saviour could bring little help to those entrusted to them, for scarcely did one single Gentile believe in God. But now whole nations come to the faith of Jesus.

Now this place contains a mystery. For there are two images in man, one which he received from God, as it is written, Let us make man in our own image: (Gen. 1:26.) another from the enemy, which he has contracted through disobedience and sin, allured and won by the enticing baits of the prince of this world. For as the penny has the image of the emperor of the world, so he who does the works of the power of darkness, bears the image of Him whose works he doth. He says then, Render unto Cæsar the things which be Cæsar's, that is, cast away the earthly image, that ye may be able, by putting on the heavenly image, to render unto God the things which be God's, namely, to love God. Which things Moses says God requires of us. (Deut. 10:12.) But God makes this demand of us, not because He has need that we should give Him any thing, but that, when we have given, He might grant us this very same…

"The good tree" is the Holy Spirit. The "bad tree" is the devil and his underlings. The person who has the Holy Spirit manifests the fruits of the Spirit, which the apostle describes when he says, "The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control." The one who has the opposing power brings forth briars and thistles, the passions of dishonor.

"Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" This which she says, "whence is this to me?" she does not say out of ignorance—and least of all when full of the Holy Spirit, as though she did not know that according to the will of God the mother of the Lord had come to her; but she speaks in this sense: what good have I done? what works of mine are so great that the mother of the Lord should come to me? through what righteousness, by what good deeds, by what fidelity of mind have I merited this, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 7

quotes.quote: "To show mercy toward our fathers" — I think that at the coming of the Lord the Savior both Abraham and Isaac and Jacob enjoyed the mercy of God. For it is not credible that those who earlier saw his day and rejoiced should afterward, at his coming and his birth from the Virgin, have received no benefit. And why do I speak of the patriarchs? Following the authority of the Scriptures, I will boldly ascend to higher things, since the presence of the Lord Jesus and his dispensation profited not only things earthly but also things heavenly. Whence the Apostle also says: "making peace through the blood of his cross, whether upon the earth or in the heavens". But if in heaven and on earth the presence of the Lord was of profit, why should you be afraid to say that his coming profited even the greater ones, so that this might be fulfilled which is said: "to show mercy toward our fathers, and…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 10

quotes.quote: Interest on the Word of God is having in life and deeds things that the Word of God has commanded. When you hear the Word, if you use it and act according to those words that you hear and live according to these words, then you are preparing interest for the Lord. Each of you can make ten talents from five. You will then hear from the Lord, "Well done, good and faithful servant, you shall have power over ten cities." Beware of this, fearing that any one of you may gather "in a napkin" or bury "in the earth" the money that has been received. You know well the nature of the outcome for this kind of man when the Lord comes.

What you have offered to God you shall receive back multiplied. Something like this, although put in another way, is related in the Gospels when in a parable someone received a pound that he might engage in business, and the master of the house demanded the money. If you have caused five to be multiplied to ten, then they are given to you. Hear what Scripture says, "Take his pound, and give it to him who has ten pounds."We therefore appear at least to engage in business for the Lord, but the profits of the business go to us. We appear to offer sacrifice to the Lord, but the things we offer are given back to us. God does not need anything, but he wants us to be rich. He desires our progress through each, individual thing.

But indeed, when the Savior was asked by the Pharisees about the kingdom of God, "when it would come", he replied: "The kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor do they say: behold, here, or behold, there. For the kingdom of God is within you". The Savior does not say to all: "the kingdom of God is within you", since in sinners there is the kingdom of sin, and without any ambiguity either the kingdom of God rules in our heart or the kingdom of sin. Whence, whether it be the things we do, or the things we speak, or the things we think, let us contemplate them more attentively, and then we shall see whether the dominion of God reigns in us or the dominion of sins. The Apostle, knowing that this diversity exists, admonishes certain people, saying: "let not sin reign in your mortal body". If any one of us desires the kingdom of God, he is ruled by it; if anyone is tormented by the…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 36

quotes.quote: And when they sought him, they did not find him "among their kinsfolk". For human kinship could not contain the Son of God. They did not find him "among their acquaintances", because the divine power was greater than mortal acquaintance and knowledge.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 19

quotes.quote: "For behold, as soon as thy greeting came into my ears, the infant leaped for exultation in my womb". Holy was the soul of blessed John, and while still enclosed in his mother's womb and yet to come into the world he knew Him whom Israel did not know; whence he "leaped", and not simply "leaped", but "for joy". For he had perceived that his Lord had come to sanctify His servant, before he came forth from his mother's belly.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 7

quotes.quote: No one that remains in his old state, and forsakes not his old habits and practices, can rightly come to be baptized; whoever then wishes to be baptized, let him go forth. Hence are those words significantly spoken, And he said unto the multitude that went forth to be baptized of him. To the multitudes then who are going forth to the laver of baptism, He speaks the following words, for if they had already gone forth, He would not have said, O generation of vipers.

But this too must be attended to, that John speaks "to the peoples going out" to baptism. If anyone wishes to be baptized, let him go out; for one remaining in his former state and not leaving his ways and his custom by no means comes rightly to baptism. And that you may understand what it is to go out to baptism, receive the testimony and hearken to the words in which God speaks to Abraham: "go out from your land" and the rest. And so, as the crowds were going out to the washing—not having gone out, but only striving to go out—John speaks the things that follow. For if they had already gone out, he would never have said to them: "brood of vipers". Whatever things, therefore, he speaks to them, he speaks also to you, O catechumens, male and female, who are preparing to come to baptism. Consider whether perhaps it may be said also to you: "brood of vipers"; for if you too have some…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 22

quotes.quote: For this reason it seems to me that the Savior answered the Nazarenes who questioned him consequently and in due order: "no prophet is accepted in his own homeland". And I think that what is said is more true according to the sacred meaning than according to the letter. Granted that Jeremiah too was not accepted in Anathoth his homeland, and Isaiah, whatever his homeland was, and the rest of the prophets; but it seems to me better to understand it thus, that we should say the homeland of all the prophets was the people of the circumcision, and that this people did not receive the prophets and their prophecies, whereas the nations, which had been far from the prophets and had no knowledge of them, received the prophecy of Jesus Christ. "No prophet" therefore "is accepted in his own homeland", that is, among the people of the Jews. But we, who were strangers to the covenant and foreigners…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 33

quotes.quote: But John, who had commenced his Gospel from God, saying, In the beginning was the Word, did not describe the temptation of the Lord, because God can not be tempted, of whom he wrote. But because in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke the human generations are given, and in Mark it is man who is tempted, therefore Matthew, Luke, and Mark have described the temptation of the Lord.

He either then says this concerning that time when God shall judge the secrets of men, or He says it because however much a man may endeavour to hide the good deeds of another by discredit, good of its own nature cannot be concealed.

For our "proof" extends not only as far as blows, but reaches even to the shedding of blood, because Christ also, whom we follow, poured out His blood for our redemption, that from it we might come forth washed in our own blood. For the baptism of blood alone is what renders us purer than the baptism of water rendered us. And this I do not presume of myself, but Scripture reports it, the Lord saying to His disciples: "I have a baptism to be baptized with, which you know not. And how am I pressed until it be accomplished?" You see, then, that He named the shedding of His blood a "baptism." And if in saying these things I give no offense, I fear that this baptism may be more eminent than that baptism which is handed on through water. For of that one, once received, very few are so blessed as to have been able to keep it unstained even to the end of life; but whoever has been baptized with…

(in Cant. 1:2.) But why does he say that many prophets desired, and not all? Because it is said of Abraham, That he saw the day of Christ and was glad, (John 8:56.) which sight not many, but few attained to; but there were other prophets and just men not so great as to reach to Abraham's vision, and the experience of the Apostles, who, He says, saw not, but desired to see.

But he who would adapt his lantern to the more perfect disciples of Christ, must persuade us by those things which were spoken of John, for he was a burning and a shining light. (John 5:35.) It becomes not him then who lights the light of reason in his soul to hide it under a bed where men sleep, nor under any vessel, for he who does this provides not for those who enter the house for whom the candle is prepared, but they must set it upon a candlestick, that is, the whole Church.

Scripture does not say this about a tangible lamp but about a comprehensible one. One does not "light" the lamp and conceal it "with a vessel" or put it "under a bed, but on the lamp stand" within himself. The vessels of the house are the powers of the soul. The bed is the body. "Those who go in" are those who hear the teacher.…He calls the holy church a "lamp stand." By its proclamation, the Word of God gives light to all who are in this world and illuminates those in the house with the rays of the truth, filling the minds of all with divine knowledge.

There follows: "and all flesh shall see the salvation of God". You were once "flesh", and you who were once "flesh"—nay, to speak more wondrously, while you are still in the flesh—you see "the salvation of God". But what it may mean, that it is said "all flesh", in that none is excepted who does not see "the salvation of God", I leave to be understood by those who know how to search out the mysteries and veins of the Scriptures.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 22

quotes.quote:
Both by the angel and the multitude of the heavenly host, by the shepherds also, and Simeon.

But they who look deeper into the matter may say, that since the genealogy is deduced from David to Joseph, therefore lest Joseph should seem to be mentioned for no purpose, as not being the father of the Saviour, he was called His father, that the genealogy might maintain its place.

"And", he says, "his father and mother were marveling over these things, which were said of him". Let us gather together into one the things that were said and written about Jesus at his birth, and then we shall be able to know that each single one is worthy of wonder. For which reason both the father was marveling — for so Joseph too was called, because he was a foster-father — the mother also was marveling over all the things "which were said of him". What then are the things that rumor had spread abroad concerning the little child Jesus? "There were shepherds in that region, keeping watch and observing the night-watches over their flock." At the very hour of Jesus' birth an angel came and said to them: "I announce to you great joy: go, and you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling-cloths and laid in a manger". The angel had not yet finished his words, and behold, "a multitude of…

quotes.quote: Luke, who wrote: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore also that which will be born holy will be called the Son of God", and who plainly handed down to us that Jesus was the son of a virgin and was not conceived of human seed, this same Luke bore witness that Joseph was his father, saying: "And his father and mother were marveling at the things that were said of him". What reason, then, was there that he should record as father one who was not the father? He who is content with a simple exposition will say: the Holy Spirit honored him with the title of father, because he had nourished the Savior. But he who inquires into something more profound can say: since the order of generation is traced from David down to Joseph, lest Joseph seem to be named in vain — he who had not been the father of the Savior — in order that the order…

quotes.quote: Or he increased in spirit, remaining not in the same measure in which he had begun, but the Spirit was ever growing in him. His will ever tending to better things, was making its own advances, and his mind ever contemplating something more divine, while his memory was exercising itself, that it might lay up more and more things in its treasury, and more firmly retain them. But he adds, And he waxed strong. For human nature is weak, as we learn, the flesh is weak. (Matt. 26:41.) It must therefore be made strong by the Spirit, for the Spirit is ready. Many wax strong in the flesh, but the wrestler of God must be strengthened by the Spirit that he may crush the wisdom of the flesh. He retires therefore to escape the noise of cities, and the thronging of the people. For it follows, And he was in the deserts. Where the air is purer, the sky more clear, and God a closer friend, that as the…

In the holy Scriptures "to grow" is spoken of in two ways: one bodily, where the human will avails nothing, the other spiritually, where the cause of growing rests upon human effort. It is of this, then — the second we set down, that is, the spiritual — that the evangelist now speaks: "but the child grew and was strengthened in spirit". What he says means this: "he grew in spirit", and did not remain in the same measure in which he had begun, but the spirit always grew in him, and, as the spirit increased through each hour and moment, his soul too received its increases. And not only the soul, but the senses and the mind as well followed the growth of the spirit. That which God commands: "increase and multiply" — those who take it simply and according to the letter, I do not know how they can explain it. For granted that "multiply" refers to number, so that, while they become more than…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 11

quotes.quote: Luke says, "Forgive us our sins," since sins are associated with our debts if we have not paid them. He says the same thing as Matthew but does not seem to leave room for the person who wishes to forgive debtors only if they repent. He says that our Savior has given the law that we should add to our prayer, "For we ourselves forgive every one who is indebted to us." Surely we all have authority to forgive sins against ourselves. This is clear from "as we forgive our debtors" and from "for we ourselves forgive every one who is indebted to us." The person inspired by Jesus and known by his fruits, as the apostles were, has received the Holy Spirit. He has become spiritual by being led by the Spirit to do everything by reason as a child of God. This person forgives whatever God forgives and retains sins that cannot be healed, serving God as the prophets by not speaking his own words but…

Let us not suppose that this refers to our bodily enemies, but our ghostly. For the Lord Jesus came mighty in battle (Ps. 24:8) to destroy all our enemies, that He might deliver us from their snares and temptation.

"Salvation from our enemies". Let us not now suppose that this is said of bodily enemies, but of spiritual ones. For the Lord Jesus came, "mighty in battle", to destroy all our enemies, that he might free us from their snares: from the hand of all our enemies "and from the hand of all who hate us".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 10

quotes.quote:
It is written, then, of John: "he shall be great in the sight of the Lord". This, which is said—"he shall be great in the sight of the Lord"—shows the greatness of John's soul, which lies open to the eyes of God; and there is something lesser, which is properly beheld in the virtue of the soul. Thus I understand also that which is said in the Gospel: "do not despise one of these least ones", who are in the Church. "Least" there is understood in distinction from the greater. I am not commanded not to despise the one who is great, because he who is great cannot be despised, but it is said to me: "do not despise one of the least". And that you may know that "least" and "little" is not said by chance, but with the reasoning we have set forth, it is written: "whoever shall scandalize one of these least ones".

The "least" one is scandalized; the great one cannot sustain a scandal. There…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 4

quotes.quote: But our Jerusalem is also wept over, because after sin enemies surround it, (that is, wicked spirits,) and cast a trench round it to besiege it, and leave not a stone behind; especially when a man after long continency, after years of chastity, is overcome, and enticed by the blandishments of the flesh, has lost his fortitude and his modesty, and has committed fornication, they will not leave on him one stone upon another, according to Ezekiel, His former righteousness I will not remember. (Ezek 18:24.)

It was meet that more deference should be paid to John than to other men, for he lived such as no other man. Wherefore indeed most rightly did they regard him with affection, only they kept not within due bounds; hence it is said, But while the people were expecting whether he were the Christ.

But love is dangerous when it is uncontrolled. For he who loves any one ought to consider the nature and causes of loving, and not to love more than the object deserves. For if he pass the due measure and bounds of love, both he who loves, and he who is loved, will be in sin.

Even love has its danger, if it exceed due measure. For whoever loves someone ought to consider the nature and the reasons for loving, and not to love him more than he deserves. For if love should overstep its measure and limit, both the one who loves and the one who is loved will be in sin. That this may become clearer, let us set forth an example. The people marveled at John and loved him, and it was truly a wonder deserving that more honor be paid to him than to the rest of men, since he had lived otherwise than all mortals. We are none of us content with simple food, but we take delight in a variety of dishes; a single kind of wine does not suffice us to drink, and we purchase wines of various flavors; but John always fed on "locusts", always on "wild honey", and was content with simple and meager food, lest his body should grow fat with richer viands and be weighed down with dainty…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 25

quotes.quote:
But because they came in haste, and not with loitering steps, it follows, They found Mary, (i. e. her who had brought Jesus into the, world,) and Joseph, (i. e. the guardian of our Lord's birth,) and the babe lying in the manger, (i. e. the Saviour Himself.)

That was the manger which Israel knew not, according to those words of Isaiah, The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib. (Isa. 3:1.)

"Whoever seeks", he says, "to save his soul will lose it, and whoever loses it will save it". The martyrs seek "to save their soul"; and for this reason they lose it, in order to save it. But those who wish "to save their soul" and do not "lose" it, these "lose both body and soul" alike "in hell". Wherefore, he says, "do not fear those who can kill the body, but rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell". This much we have said briefly on the point at hand, according to the strength of our talent; but "the natural man does not receive the things that are of the Spirit", and therefore he cannot be saved. "A natural body is sown, a spiritual body rises". Further, "he who cleaves to the Lord becomes one spirit" with him. If, then, "he who is joined to the Lord", though he was natural, is by that very thing turned into a spiritual man and "is one spirit", let us too lose…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 36

quotes.quote:
But from the fig tree learn a parable: for when its branch has now become tender and puts forth leaves, know that summer is near; so also you, when you shall see all these things, know that it is near, at the door. Amen I say to you, that this generation shall not pass away, until all things be done. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

How the comparison of the things that have been said can be understood from the fig tree, we shall expound according to our ability: lest perhaps this whole world and its consummation be likened to a fig tree, and each one of those setting out toward the blessed life, so as to see in himself the glorious and perfect coming of Christ's word, be held to be like a fig tree. For just as the fig tree in the time of winter indeed has in itself the life-giving power, but has it hidden and not sufficiently manifest, and afterward,…

(in Luc. 37.) The disciples next place their garments upon the ass, and cause the Saviour to sit thereon, inasmuch as they take upon themselves the word of God, and make it to rest upon the souls of their hearers. They divest themselves of their garments, and strew them in the way, for the clothing of the Apostles is their good works. And truly does the ass loosened by the disciples and carrying Jesus, walk upon the garments of the Apostles, when it imitates their doctrine. Which of us is so blessed, that Jesus should rest upon him?

Then the disciples put "their garments upon the donkey" and make the Savior sit upon it. They take up the Word of God and set it upon the souls of the hearers. They strip off their garments, they "spread" them "in the way". Upon us are the garments of the apostles; their good works are our adornments: the apostles wish their garments to be trodden by us. And indeed the donkey, untied by the disciples and bearing Jesus, walks upon the garments of the apostles when it imitates their teaching and their life.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 37

quotes.quote:
By the poor He means the Gentile nations, for they were poor, possessing nothing at all, having neither God, nor Law, nor Prophets, nor justice, and the other virtues.

For what had been so shattered and dashed about as man, who was set at liberty by Jesus and healed?

Let us therefore contemplate what those things are which he spoke in the prophet and afterward sounds forth about himself in the synagogue. "He sent me", it says, "to evangelize the poor". The "poor" signifies the nations; for these were "poor", possessing nothing at all, not God, not the law, not the prophets, not justice and the remaining virtues. For which cause God sent him to announce to the poor: "to preach release to the captives". Captives we were, whom for so many years Satan had bound, holding us captive and subject to himself. Jesus came "to preach release to the captives and to the blind, that they might see"; for indeed by the word and preaching of his teaching the blind see. Let the preaching therefore be understood ἀπὸ κοινοῦ (in common), not only over the captives, but also over the blind. "To send forth the broken into liberty". What was ever so broken and crushed as…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 32

quotes.quote: (in Matt. tom. 12.) Now His disciples being unable to bear this, fell down, humbled under the mighty hand of God, greatly afraid since they knew what was said to Moses, No man shall see my face, and lice. Hence it follows, And they feared as they entered into the cloud.

Do you wish to see that Moses is always with Jesus, that is, the law with the gospels? Let the gospel teach you that, when Jesus "had been transfigured" into glory, also "Moses and Elijah appeared" together with him in glory, so that you may know that the law and the prophets and the gospels always come into one and remain in one glory. Finally Peter too, when he wished to make "three tabernacles" for them, is marked for his lack of skill, as one "who knew not what he said". For to the law and the prophets and the gospel there is not three tabernacles, but one, which is the church of God.

(non occ.) Zacharias is by interpretation "remembering God," but John signifies "pointing to." Now "memory" relates to something absent, "pointing to," to something present. But John was not about to set forth the memory of God as absent, but with his finger to point him out as present, saying, Behold the Lamb of God.

He prays for those who pray and appeals with those who appeal. He does not, however, pray for servants who do not pray continuously through him. He will not be the Advocate with God for his own if they are not obedient to his instructions that they always should pray and not lose heart. It says, "And he told them a parable to the effect that they should always pray and not lose heart. In a certain city there was a judge, etc." … Who would hesitate a moment to be persuaded to pray if he believes that the mouth of Jesus cannot lie, when he says, "Ask, and it will be given you … for everyone who asks, receives"?

Next we read: "But for Elizabeth the time was fulfilled that she should bring forth, and she bore a son". Many think it is said superfluously: "But for Elizabeth the time was fulfilled that she should bring forth, and she bore a son". For what woman can bring forth unless she has first fulfilled the time of bringing forth? But whoever contemplates the Scriptures most diligently and hears Paul saying: "attend to the reading", observing both in the Old and in the New Testament, if anywhere he might find it written at the birth of a sinner: "the time was fulfilled that she should bring forth", he will never at all find it. But wherever a just man is born, there the days are fulfilled, there the coming into the world is fulfilled. The birth of the just has fullness, but the nativity of a sinner has, so to speak, emptiness and hollowness. So much for what is written: "the time was fulfilled…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 9

quotes.quote: But to those that fear Him, He hath done mighty things with His arm; though thou comest weak to God, if thou hast feared Him thou shalt obtain the promised strength.

"For those who fear him he has done a mighty deed with his arm". Though you come to the Lord weak, if you have feared him, you will be able to hear the promise which the Lord pledges to you on account of your fear of him. What is this promise? "For those who fear him", she says, "he has done a mighty deed". A mighty deed, or dominion, is royal power. For indeed κράτος, which we may call "dominion", is so named from the fact that it holds command, or contains all things under itself. If therefore you have feared the Lord, he gives you strength or dominion, he gives you a kingdom, so that, made subject to the "King of kings", you may possess "the kingdom of heaven" in Christ Jesus: to whom is glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 8

quotes.quote: (vid. etiam Tit. Bos.) He was not filled with the Spirit, until she stood near him who bore Christ in her womb. Then indeed he was both filled with the Spirit, and leaping imparted the grace to his mother; as it follows, And Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. But we cannot doubt that she who was then filled with the Holy Spirit, was filled because of her son.

There is therefore no doubt that she who then "was filled with the Holy Spirit" was "filled" on account of her son! For the mother did not first merit the Holy Spirit, but rather, when John, still enclosed in the womb, had received the Holy Spirit, then she too, after the sanctification of her son, "was filled with the Holy Spirit". You will be able to believe this if you learn something similar also concerning the Savior. Blessed Mary is found—as we have discovered in a good number of copies—to prophesy. For we are not unaware that, according to other manuscripts, it is Elizabeth who utters these words in prophecy. Mary, then, was filled with the Holy Spirit at that time when she began to have the Savior in her womb. For as soon as she received the Holy Spirit, the fashioner of the Lord's body, and the Son of God began to be in her womb, she herself too was filled with the Holy Spirit.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 7

quotes.quote: When we also are silent, (that is, when the love of many waxeth cold,) the stones cry out, for God can from stones raise up children to Abraham.

Seeing this, the Pharisees said to the Lord: "rebuke them"; to whom he answered: "If these keep silent, the stones will cry out". When we speak, the stones are silent; when we keep silent, the stones cry out; "for the Lord is able to raise up from these stones sons of Abraham". At what time shall we keep silent? When "the charity of many shall have grown cold", when that which was foretold by the Savior shall have been fulfilled: "do you think that the Son of man, when he comes, will find faith upon the earth?" Therefore let us entreat the Lord's mercy, lest, while we are silent, the stones cry out, but let us speak and praise God in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit: to whom is glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 37

quotes.quote: He is not found as soon as sought for, for Jesus was not among His kinsfolk and relations, among those who are joined to Him in the flesh, nor in the company of the multitude can He be found. Learn where those who seek Him find Him, not every where, but in the temple. And do thou then seek Jesus in the temple of God. Seek Him in the Church, and seek Him among the masters who are in the temple. For if thou wilt so seek Him, thou shalt find Him. They found Him not among His kinsfolk, for human relations could not comprehend the Son of God; not among His acquaintance, for He passes far beyond all human knowledge and understanding. Where then do they find Him? In the temple! If at any time thou seek the Son of God, seek Him first in the temple, thither go up, and verily shalt thou find Christ, the Word, and the Wisdom, (i. e. the Son of God.)

They seek "among their kinsfolk", they seek "in the company", they seek "among their acquaintances", and in all these they do not find him. Jesus, then, is sought by his parents, by the father who had been his nurse and companion when he went down to Egypt, and yet he is not found immediately when he is sought. For Jesus is not found among relatives and kinsmen of the flesh, not among those who are joined to him bodily. In the company of many my Jesus cannot be found.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 18

quotes.quote:
They who explain this simply, may say that He came for the fall of unbelievers, and the rising again of believers.

The careful interpreter will say, that no one falls who was not before standing. Tell me then, who were they who stood, for whose fall Christ came?

There is also a deeper meaning aimed against those who raise their voices against their Creator, saying, Behold the God of the Law and the Prophets of what sort He is! He says, I kill, and I make alive. (Deut. 32:39.) If God then is a bloody judge and a cruel master, it is most plain that Jesus is His Son, since the same things here are written of Him, namely, that he comes for the fall and rising again of many.

But we must take care lest by chance the Saviour should not come to some equally for the fall and rising again; for when I stood in sin, it was first good for me to fall, and die to sin. Lastly, Prophets and Saints…

Then the Scripture says: "Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: Behold, this one is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign that shall be contradicted. And a sword shall pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts out of many hearts may be revealed". In what way the Savior came "for the ruin and for the resurrection of many" is to be contemplated. He who expounds simply can say that he came "for the ruin" of unbelievers and "for the resurrection" of believers. But he who is a careful interpreter says that by no means does one fall who has not first stood. Give me, then, who that one was who stood, and for whose "ruin" the Savior came, and also him who rises up. For surely he rises up who had before fallen. And so we must see whether perhaps the Savior did not come "for the ruin" of some and "for the resurrection" of others, but came for…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 17

quotes.quote: What does this mean which he says: "behold, this one is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel"? To this I have found something similar written in the Gospel according to John: "for judgment I have come into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may be made blind". Therefore, just as he came for judgment, that "those who do not see" of the nations "might see", and those who saw before, of Israel, "might be made blind", so he came "for the fall and rising of many". For at the coming of the Lord the Savior, those who had stood before fell down, and those who had fallen rose up. This is one interpretation of that which was said: "behold, this one is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel". But there is also something deeper to be understood against those especially who bark against the Creator, and, gathering together from here and there out of the…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 16

quotes.quote: And he teaches that he who was going down was neighbor to no one except to him who was willing to keep the precepts and to prepare himself, so as to be neighbor to every man who is in need of aid. For this is what is set down at the end after the parable: "Which of these three seems to you to be neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?" For neither the priest nor the Levite was his neighbor, but, as the doctor of the law himself also answered, "he who did mercy" was his neighbor. Whence it is also said by the Savior: "Go, and you also do likewise".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 34

quotes.quote: Truly this "guardian" of souls is nearer than the law and the prophets — he "who did mercy to him who had fallen among robbers" — and he appeared as his "neighbor" not so much by word as by deed. Since, therefore, it is possible, according to that which is said: "Be imitators of me, as I also am of Christ", for us to imitate Christ and to have mercy on those who "have fallen among robbers", to approach them, to bind up their wounds, to pour in oil and wine, to set them upon our own beast and to bear their burdens — for this reason the Son of God, exhorting us to such things, speaks not so much to the doctor of the law as to us all also: "Go, and you also do likewise". And if we shall do likewise, we shall attain eternal life in Christ Jesus: to whom is glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 34

quotes.quote:
For when Jesus had come and sent His Spirit, every valley was filled with good works, and the fruits of the Holy Spirit, which if thou hast, thou wilt not only cease to become a valley, but will begin also to be a mountain of God.

Or you may understand the mountains and hills to be the hostile powers, which have been overthrown by the coming of Christ.

Let us see what things are foretold at the coming of Christ, among which first it is written concerning John: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: prepare the way of the Lord, make straight his paths". And what follows pertains properly to the Lord the Savior. For "every valley" was not "filled" by John, but by the Lord the Savior. Let each one consider himself, what he was before he believed, and then he will observe that he was a lowly valley, a headlong valley plunged into the depths. But when the Lord Jesus came and sent the Holy Spirit as his vicar, "every valley" was "filled". And it was "filled" with good works and with the fruits of the Holy Spirit. Love does not permit a valley to remain in you, for, if you have peace and patience and goodness, not only will you cease to be a "valley", but you will even begin to be a "mountain" of God. We see this happening and being…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 22

quotes.quote: And it came to pass that on the same road there went down first a "priest", then a "Levite", who had perhaps done certain good things to other men, yet not to this one who had gone down "from Jerusalem to Jericho". For the "priest" saw him — the law, I think — the "Levite" saw him — the prophetic word, as I suppose — and when they had seen him, they passed by and left him.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 34

quotes.quote: Although these things are said reasonably and beautifully, it is nevertheless not to be supposed that they pertain to every man. For not every man "goes down from Jerusalem to Jericho", nor do all on that account tarry in the present age, even though he who "was sent because of the lost sheep" — "of the house of Israel" — came. The man, therefore, who "went down from Jerusalem to Jericho", because he himself willed to go down, for that reason "fell among robbers". But the robbers are none other than those of whom the Savior says: "all who came before me were thieves and robbers". Yet he fell not among thieves, but among "robbers" much more wicked than thieves, who, when he was going down "from Jerusalem" and had fallen among them, "stripped him and laid blows upon him". What are the blows, what the wounds, by which the man was wounded? Vices and sins. Then, because the robbers who had…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 34

quotes.quote: The devil therefore says to the Lord: You have come for this, to fight against me and to take from my dominion those whom I now hold subject. I do not wish you to contend, I do not wish you to strive, lest you have any trouble in the struggle. There is one thing that I beg: "falling down, adore me", and receive all the kingdom that I hold. But our Lord and Savior does indeed wish to reign and to have all the nations subject to himself, that they may serve justice, truth, and the other virtues; yet he wishes to reign as justice itself, so that he may reign without sin, so that he may do nothing unseemly, and he does not wish to be crowned without labor by being subject to the devil, nor so to reign over the rest that he himself should be ruled by the devil. Whence he speaks to him: "it is written: You shall adore the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve". All these, he says, I…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 30

quotes.quote: But all these things were mentioned first, in order that after the recovery of sight from blindness, after deliverance from captivity, after being healed of divers wounds, we might come to the acceptable year of the Lord. As it follows, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. Some say that, according to the simple meaning of the word, the Saviour preached the Gospel throughout Judæa in one year, and that this is what is meant by preaching the acceptable year of the Lord. Or, the acceptable year of the Lord is the whole time of the Church, during which while present in the body, it is absent from the Lord.

"To preach the acceptable year of the Lord". According to the simple understanding they say that the Savior preached the Gospel in Judea for one year, and that this is what is said: "to preach the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution", unless perhaps the divine word signifies something of a mystery in the preaching of the year of the Lord. For there are to be other days, not such as we now discern in the world, and other months, and a different order of the Kalends. Just therefore as those are other, so also the year of the Lord to come is pleasing. But all these things have been foretold, that after sight from blindness, after liberty from chains, after health from diverse wounds, we may come to the "acceptable year of the Lord".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 32

quotes.quote: He who has married a wife is he who is joined to the flesh, a lover of pleasure rather than of God. (1 Tim. 3:4.)

But if I have searched out something more deeply, I will observe how great is the advance signified by saying: "because he who is mighty has done great things for me": for since "everyone who humbles himself will be exalted", and God "has looked upon the lowliness" of blessed Mary, therefore "he who is mighty has done" for her "great things, and holy is his name".
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 8

quotes.quote: When the prophetic word was sent to the Jews alone, Jewish kings were set at the heading. For example: "The vision which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw against Judea and against Jerusalem, in the reign of Uzziah and Jotham and Ahaz and Hezekiah"; nor do I see anyone else, apart from the kings of Judea, designated in Isaiah's time. In certain of the prophets we read also the kings of Israel, as in that place: "and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel". But when the mystery of the Gospel was to be proclaimed and the Gospel was to be spread throughout the whole world, whose herald John was in the wilderness, and the empire of Tiberius ruled the world, then "in the fifteenth year" of him "the word of the Lord" is described as having "come to John". And if salvation had had to be announced only to those who were about to believe from among the nations, and Israel had had to…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 21

quotes.quote: (in Matt. tom. 12.) A man also denies himself when by a sufficient alteration of manners or a good conversation he changes a life of habitual wickedness. He who has long lived in lasciviousness, abandons his lustful self when he becomes chaste, and in like manner a forsaking of any crimes is a denial of one's self.

For if Mary had known that such a word had been spoken to any other as well — for she had knowledge of the Law and was holy and had come to know the oracles of the prophets by daily meditation — the greeting would never have terrified her as something strange.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 6

quotes.quote: Whence it also seems marvelous that Mary's offering did not have the first victim, that is, "a yearling lamb," but the second, as one whose "hand did not suffice" for the first. For thus it is written concerning her: there came, it says, her parents, "that they might offer" for him "a victim, according to that which is written in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons." But in this too is shown to be true that which is written, that Christ Jesus, "whereas he was rich, became poor." Therefore for this reason he both chose a poor mother, of whom he would be born, and a poor fatherland, of which it is said: "And thou, Bethlehem, art the least among the thousands of Judah," and the rest.

For this reason, because "every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord", he was brought "to Jerusalem", that he might appear before the sight of God, and on account of that which follows: "that a gift might be given for him, according to what is written in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons". We see a pair of turtledoves and two young pigeons offered for the Savior. I even think those birds blessed, which were offered for the birth of the Lord; and just as I marvel at Balaam's ass and heap up her happiness, because she was worthy not only to see the angel of God, but also, with her mouth unlocked, to break forth into human speech, so much more do I proclaim and exalt these birds, that they were offered for our Lord and Savior before the altar. "That they might offer for him a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons". Perhaps I may seem to…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 14

quotes.quote: To those who attentively consider it, there seems to be expressed a kind of sacrament, in its being necessary that Christ should be put down in the registration of the whole world; in order that His name being written with all, He might sanctify all, and being placed in the census with the whole world, He might impart to the world the communion of Himself.

[Scripture] says that man was made in the image of God; and in him are manifestly to be discovered traces of the divine image, not by any appearance of the bodily frame, which is corruptible, but by mental wisdom, by justice, moderation, virtue, wisdom, discipline; in fine, by the whole band of virtues, which are innate in the essence of God, and which may enter into man by diligence and imitation of God; as the Lord also intimates in the Gospel, when He says, "Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful; " and, "Be ye perfect, even as your Father also is perfect." From which it is clearly shown that all these virtues are perpetually in God, and that they can never approach to or depart from Him, whereas by men they are acquired only slowly, and one by one.

Our Lord and Savior is born in Bethlehem, and "a multitude of the heavenly host" praises God and says: "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among men of good will". Now the "multitude of the heavenly host" speaks these words because it had already failed to furnish men with help, and it saw that it could not fulfill the work that had been entrusted to it apart from him who was truly able to save and even to assist the presiding powers themselves, so that men might be saved. Therefore, just as it is written in the Gospel that certain men, plowing the sea with their oars against contrary winds, were already exhausted and, laboring for twenty-five or thirty stadia, could not reach the harbor, and afterward the Lord came upon them and made the swelling waves grow calm, and freed the ship, whose sides were being flooded on this side and that, from the impending danger — so…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 13

quotes.quote: It was ordered about sun-set, that is, when the day was gone, that they should bring them out, either because during the day they were employed about other things, or because they thought that it was not lawful to heal on the sabbath. But He healed them, as it follows, But he laid his hands upon every one of them.

Let us then ascend with the Lord united to us, to the upper part in which is the guestchamber, which is shown by the understanding, that is, the goodman of the house, to every one of the disciples of Christ. But this upper room of our house must be large enough to receive Jesus the Word of God, who is not comprehended but by those who are greater in comprehension. And this chamber must be made ready by the goodman of the house, (that is, the understanding,) for the Son of God, and it must be cleaned, wholly purged of the filth of malice. The master of the house also must not be any common person having a known name. Hence He says mystically in Matthew, Go ye to such a one.

I think that at the coming of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, both Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, were partakers of His mercy. For it is not to be believed, that they who had before seen His day, and were glad, should afterwards derive no advantage from His coming, since it is written, Having made peace through the blood of his Cross, whether in earth or in heaven. (Coloss. 1:20.)

But some one may seek to know, how it comes that they who pray are not heard? To which we must answer, that whose sets about seeking in the right way, omitting none of those things which avail to the obtaining of our requests, shall really receive what he has prayed to be given him. But if a man turns away from the object of a right petition, and asks not as it becomes him, he does not ask. And therefore it is, that when he does not receive, as is here promised, there is no falsehood. For so also when a master says, "Whoever will come to me, he shall receive the gift of instruction;" we understand it to imply a person going in real earnest to a master, that he may zealously and diligently devote himself to his teaching. Hence too James says, Ye ask and receive not, because ye ask amiss, (James 4:3.) namely, for the sake of vain pleasures. But some one will say, Nay, when men ask to…

He who believes that the mouth of Jesus cannot lie would hesitate a moment to be persuaded to pray, when he says, "Ask, and it will be given you … for everyone who asks, receives." When we ask for the living bread, the good Father certainly gives him (and not the stone that his adversary wishes to give to Jesus and his disciples for food) to those who have received the Spirit of sonship from the Father. The Father gives a good gift, raining it down from heaven for those who ask him.

That is, If thy material body, when the light of a candle shines upon it, is made full of light, so that not one of thy members is any longer in darkness; much more when thou sinnest not, shall thy whole spiritual body be so full of light, that its brightness may be compared to the shining of a candle, while the light which was in the body, and which used to be darkness, is directed whithersoever the understanding may command.

Or, to view the whole in another light. Two kings are earnestly contending for a kingdom; The king of sin who reigneth over sinners, that is, the devil; The king of righteousness who ruleth the righteous, that is, Christ. The devil, knowing that Christ had come to take away his kingdom, shows Him all the kingdoms of the world; not the kingdoms of the Persians and of the Medes, but his own kingdom whereby he reigned in the world, whereby some are under the dominion of fornication, others of covetousness. And he shows Him them in a moment of time, that is, in the present course of time, which is but a moment in comparison of eternity. For the Saviour needed not to be shown for any longer time the affairs of this world, but as soon as He turned His eyes to look, He beheld sins reigning, and men made slaves to vice. The devil therefore says unto Him, Camest Thou to contend with me for…

That is, to those who are of Israel, whom he saw possessing nothing divine in them, but desolate, and vacant for him to take up his abode there; and so it follows, And when he came, he findeth it swept and garnished.

And on that account, shut up "in prison", he was anxious not about death, not about the uncertain judgment of the judge, but in his chains was thinking about Christ, whom he had proclaimed. And because he himself could not go to him, he sends his disciples to inquire: "Are you he who is to come, or do we look for another?" Take note that he taught "even in prison". For whence had he disciples even in that place, and for what reason did they persevere there, unless because even in prison he was performing the office of a master and was instructing them with divine discourses? And among these, when a question had arisen concerning Jesus, he sends some of his disciples and asks: "Are you he who is to come, or do we look for another?" The disciples return and report to their master what the Savior had commanded to be reported: armed with his words, John dies confidently for the battle and…

And when someone is in this state, it is possible that, even if he does not have the strength of the sun, yet he may be illumined by some slight brightness of the word which is a "lamp", while still indeed remaining amid evils, yet already having a purpose of better things and a watchfulness, so that his purpose, looking toward better things, may not be broken in upon. For, as we read in the Shepherd, no one quickly tastes full vessels, for they are not easily changed; but the half-full ones, because they are readily believed to be changed, are frequently tasted.

And see whether you can draw to such an understanding that which is written elsewhere: "but let your loins be girded and your lamps burning; and be you like men awaiting their lord, when he shall return"; since he who is not yet in the light and in the day of the virtues, but already offers himself to the teaching that…

And the master too comes at a certain watch and hour of the night, and perhaps the master comes to that man to whom the thief, in coming, could do nothing — namely, not being permitted to dig through the house of the one keeping watch and having a lamp lit. After which the Scripture adds: "It came to pass in those days, there went out an edict from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be enrolled. This was the first census, under Quirinius, governor of Syria". Someone may say: evangelist, how does this narrative help me — that the "first census" of the whole world took place under Caesar Augustus, and that among all the rest "Joseph too, with Mary who was betrothed to him and with child", entered his name in the register, and that, before the census was completed, Jesus was born? To one who looks more carefully a certain mystery seems to be signified: that in the enrollment of the whole world Christ too had to be registered, so that, written down with all, he might sanctify all, and, entered in the census with the world, he might offer the world communion with himself, so that after this census he might also enroll from the world,…

quotes.quote: But mystically, he who shuns vain-glory calls to a spiritual banquet the poor, that is, the ignorant, that he may enrich them; the weak, that is, those with offended consciences, that he may heal them; the lame, that is, those who have wandered from reason, that he may make their paths straight; the blind, that is, those who discern not the truth, that they may behold the true light. But it is said, They cannot recompense thee, i. e. they know not how to return an answer.

Concerning the bread a thing similar to what Matthew records of the cup is said in Luke: "With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you. I say to you that from now on I will not eat it, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God." Therefore the Savior will eat and drink that bread and paschal drink renewed "in the kingdom of God," and he will eat and drink with his disciples. For just as "he did not deem it robbery to be equal to God, but humbled himself even unto death," so he will eat the bread and drink of the generation of the vine, and he will drink it new, and by reason of his great goodness and his love of men he will eat and drink with his disciples, "when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father." The reason I suppose that Zacharias hastened to speak to his son, was because he knew that John was shortly about to be a sojourner in the wilderness, and that he himself should see him no more.

"And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High". Seeking within myself the reason why he prophesies not as though about John, but by speaking to John himself: "and you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High", and the rest — for it was superfluous to speak to one who does not hear and to make an apostrophe to a little one and a suckling — I think I can find this: that just as John was born wondrously and came into the world with an angel proclaiming it, and was poured forth upon the earth while Mary lodged three months beside Elizabeth, so also all the things that are written about him are reported to have been done wondrously. But if you doubt that one just poured forth from his mother's womb could hear his father's words and know what this is which is said to him: "and you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High", consider that what went before…

quotes.quote: Or, because without the wind the wheat and chaff cannot be separated, therefore He has the fan in His hand, which shows some to be chaff, some wheat; for when you were as the light chaff; (i. e. unbelieving,) temptation showed you to be what you knew not; but when you shall bravely endure temptation, the temptation will not make you faithful and enduring, but it will bring to light the virtue which was hid in you.

"God is a spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth". Our God too "is a consuming fire". God, therefore, is called by two names: both "spirit" and "fire": spirit for the righteous, fire for sinners. But the angels also are called spirits and fire: "he who makes", it says, "his angels spirits and his ministers a burning fire"; to the holy ones they are spirits, but to those who deserve punishments they supply fire and burning. According to which sense our Lord and Savior too, since he is "spirit", "came to send fire upon the earth"; "spirit" according to that which is written: "but when you have turned to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away", and: "the Lord is a spirit". But "he came to send fire" not upon heaven, but "upon the earth", as he himself shows when he says: "I came to send fire upon the earth, and what do I wish but that it already blaze?" For…

quotes.quote: From these words it is undoubtingly gathered, that the life which is preached according to God the Creator of the world, and the Scriptures given by Him, is life everlasting. For the Lord Himself bears testimony to the passage from Deuteronomy, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God; (Deut. 6:5.) and from Leviticus, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. (Lev. 19:18.) But these things were spoken against the followers of Valentinus, Basil, and Marcion. For what else did he wish us to do in seeking eternal life, but what is contained in the Law and the Prophets?

People of God are truly the salt of the earth. They preserve the order of the world. Society is held together as long as the salt is uncorrupted. If the salt lost its savor, it is neither suitable for the land or the manure pile. It will be thrown out and trampled underfoot. "He that has ears, let him hear" the meaning of these words. When God gives to the tempter permission to persecute us, then we suffer persecution. When God wishes us to be free from suffering even in the middle of a world that hates us, we enjoy a wonderful peace. We trust in the protection of him who said, "Be of good cheer, I have overcome the world."

John having announced the coming of Christ, was preaching the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and the other things which the Gospel history has handed down to us. But besides these he is declared to have announced others in the following words, And many other things in his exhortation preached he unto the people.

And as in the Gospel according to St. John it is related of Christ that He spoke many other things, so also in this place we must understand Luke to say the same of John the Baptist, since certain things are announced by John too great to be entrusted to writing.

He who teaches the word of the Gospel proclaims not one thing but very many. For this is what Scripture signifies when it says: "now with many other exhortations also he was proclaiming good news". And so John was preaching to the people "other" things as well, which are not written down; but the things that are written—consider how many they were. He proclaimed Christ, he pointed him out, he preached the baptism of the Holy Spirit; he taught the tax collectors salvation, the soldiers discipline, that the threshing floor is to be cleansed, that the trees are to be cut down, and the rest that the narrative of the Gospel relates. Therefore, apart from these things that are written, he is shown to have proclaimed still other things that are not written, in that it is said: "now with many other exhortations also he was proclaiming good news to the people". And just as in the Gospel…

quotes.quote: Literally, hereby is signified the quickness of the Divine foresight, which reaches even to the least things. But mystically, the five sparrows justly represent the spiritual senses, which have perception of high and heavenly things: beholding God, hearing the Divine voice, tasting of the bread of life, smelling the perfume of Christ's anointing, handling the Word of Life. And these being sold for two farthings, that is, being lightly esteemed by those who count as perishing whatever is of the Spirit, are not forgotten before God. But God is said to be forgetful of some because of their iniquities.

Here Luke speaks figuratively, as of a command given to a sensible being, saying, that the fever was commanded, and neglected not the work of Him who commanded it. Hence it follows: And she arose, and ministered unto them.
John indeed turned many, but it is the Lord's work to turn all to God their Father.

Then Scripture says that "he shall convert very many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God". John converts "very many", but the Lord not many, rather all. This is his work, that he should convert all to God the Father.

quotes.quote: Or, because the name of God is given by idolaters, and those who are in error, to idols and creatures, it has not as yet been so made holy, as to be separated from those things from which it ought to be. He teaches us therefore to pray that the name of God may be appropriated to the only true God; to whom alone belongs what follows, Thy kingdom come, to the end that may be put down all the rule, authority, and power, and kingdom of the world, together with sin which reigns in our mortal bodies.

Perhaps we should … pray … only to the God and Father of all, to whom even our Savior himself prayed, as we have explained, and to whom he taught us to pray. When he heard "teach us to pray," he did not teach us to pray to himself but to the Father by saying "Our Father in heaven and so forth." …When the saints give thanks to God in their prayers, they acknowledge through Christ Jesus the favors he has done. If it is true that one who is scrupulous about prayer should not pray to someone else who prays but rather to the Father whom our Lord Jesus taught us to address in prayers, it is especially true that no prayer should be addressed to the Father without him.

The phrase "lift up your eyes" occurs in many places in Scripture. By this expression, the divine Word admonishes us to exalt and lift up our thoughts. It invites us to elevate the insight that lies below in a rather sickly condition and is stooped and completely incapable of looking up. For instance, it is written in Isaiah, "Lift up your eyes on high and see. Who has made all these things known?"The Savior too, when he is about to deliver the Beatitudes, lifts up his eyes to the disciples and says "blessed" are such and such.

quotes.quote: A reason worthy of God's gift must be sought, as to how "Simeon, a holy man and pleasing to God", as it is written in the Gospel, "awaiting the consolation of Israel, received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not meet death before he saw the Christ of the Lord". What good did it do him to see Christ? Did he have only this in the promise, that he should see him, and gain no benefit from seeing him, or does some gift worthy of God lie hidden here, which the blessed Simeon both deserved and received? quotes.quote: Jesus "advanced in wisdom" and appeared wiser through each successive age. Was he not wise, that he should become wiser? Or was it that, since he had "emptied himself, taking the form of a servant", he was taking up again what he had laid down, and being filled again with the virtues which, a little before, upon assuming a body, he had seemed to relinquish? He "advanced", therefore, not only "in wisdom", but also "in age". There is also an advancement of age. Two ages are spoken of in the Scriptures: one of the body, which is not in our power but in the law of nature; the other of the soul, which properly lies within us, and according to which, if we will, we daily grow and come to its summit, "so that we may be no longer little children, tossed about and carried around by every wind of doctrine", but, ceasing to be "little children", may begin to be "men" and may say: "when I became a…

For just as sickness of the body makes a man's body meager and slight, but health makes it flourishing and strong, so understand that sickness of sin makes the soul too lowly and small, but the health of the inner man and the works of virtue make it great and eminent, and the more it grows in virtues, the more it renders the greatness of itself extensive. Thus do I understand that which is written of Jesus: that "he advanced in wisdom and in stature and in grace with God and men". For who among men is there who does not "advance in stature" in boyhood, that this should be written of Jesus as though it were something remarkable?
